articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake at IGN: walkthroughs, items, maps, video tips, and strategies
articles.body:
In 1998, Nintendo released The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo 64. As the first 3D Zelda game, it went on to become one of the highest rated video games ever made. Almost 30 years later, Ocarina of Time has been remade on the Nintendo Switch 2, featuring a vibrant and detailed world rebuilt from the ground up. Much of Ocarina of Time has been faithfully remade, with several new additions and features that compliment this legendary adventure.

In the land of Hyrule, a young child of the forest named Link embarks on adventure to save the land from encroaching darkness, coming to the aid of the Princess of Hyrule to protect the Sacred Realm. His journey will take him not just to every corner of the land, but through time itself. It's up to Link to take up the blade of evil's bane known as the Master Sword, and defeat the dark forces threatening all of Hyrule as he explores sprawling dungeons full of traps and tricks, using the items he finds in his travels to open up new areas and uncover secrets.

articles.title: Scarlett Johansson Says The Batman: Part 2 Role Caused 'Existential Angst'
articles.summary: While she didn’t disclose the character she’s playing, Scarlett Johansson says her role in The Batman: Part II has given her “a lot of existential angst” because it was “hard to crack."
articles.body:
While she didn’t disclose the character she’s playing, Scarlett Johansson says her role in The Batman: Part II has given her “a lot of existential angst” because it was “hard to crack.”

The Black Widow star was interviewed by Entertainment Tonight about her new movie Paper Tiger, where she was asked which of her roles in upcoming franchise films (Exorcist: Martyrs or The Batman: Part II) pushed her the most outside of her comfort zone

“Probably the role in The Batman, because it gave me a lot of existential angst, for some reason,” Johansson explained.

“It was very hard to figure out. I don’t know why, whether it was just the role or it was just where I am in my life, but it was just hard to crack it. And that’s all I can say about it.”

The Batman: Part II - Who's Who in Matt Reeves' DC Sequel

The rumor mill has suggested Johansson is playing Gilda Dent or Poison Ivy in the sequel.

Johansson isn’t the only cast member who’s been asked about The Batman: Part II in recent interviews. Robert Pattinson has praised the sequel for having " an understanding of Bruce Wayne and Batman's psychology " that he doesn't "think has been seen before."

The Batman: Part II has resumed filming in the UK under the supervision of Steven Soderbergh , who is overseeing the final stages of shooting while director Matt Reeves deals with a family matter . Reeves will resume the directing reins once the film reaches post-production.

Despite the production delays, The Batman: Part II remains scheduled to open in theaters on February 18, 2028.

articles.title: Captain Price Actor Barry Sloane Says He's the Most Qualified Person to Star in the Call of Duty Movie
articles.summary: Captain Price actor Barry Sloane wants to be in the Call of Duty movie and believes he's the most qualified person for the job.
articles.body:
Captain Price actor Barry Sloane wants to be in the Call of Duty movie and believes he's the most qualified person for the job.

When speaking with Dan Allen Gaming , Sloane was asked if he's interested in reprising his role as Price in the upcoming live-action Call of Duty film. The movie, directed by Peter Berg and written by Taylor Sheridan, is expected to be set in the Modern Warfare universe , but it's unclear if it's a new story or a direct adaptation of one of the games. With that said, it's hard to imagine a Modern Warfare movie without Price. Sloane wants in on the film and even went as far as to say he's the most qualified person on the planet to do it.

"I don't think there's anyone else on the planet who is as qualified for the job as I am," said Sloane. "Who has lived the character for almost a decade? Who understands the size of the projects, the love of that fan base, and has been on the journey with them from the get-go? Hollywood is a beast. Sometimes things are decided for certain reasons that can never be understood. But if you're asking me, would I like to do it? Absolutely, I would love to play him in a movie. 100%. That would be fantastic. But let's let the Hollywood cards fall where they land."

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Campaign Screenshots

Sloane also noted that there's been a vocal outpouring from fans to have him play Price in the film, which he massively appreciates. He noted that typically, there's a group of names that a studio wants for a role like this, and they have to go through that process themselves. Nevertheless, he believes he'd be an "asset" to the production if he were to have the opportunity.

As games have gotten increasingly realistic, they've also started to use the likenesses of the actors who play them. This has led to demand from fans that film adaptations should use the actors from the games. Of course, Hollywood might make the argument that they're not as big of a box office draw compared to a more traditional mainstream movie star. Whether Call of Duty will utilize the game's cast remains to be seen.

Spoilers for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 follow below .

Of course, if the Call of Duty movie is canonical to the games, where it falls in the timeline will dictate what characters can show up. Modern Warfare 4 brutally takes a number of characters off the board, including Captain Price. At the end of the game, the character is left to bleed out in the middle of the wilderness, with Ghost having said his goodbyes to his fallen leader. It's a tragic ending for the character, but one that felt right and leaves the future of the Modern Warfare games in question .

With that said, if the Call of Duty movie takes place within the canon, it would have to be set before Modern Warfare 4. If it's a sequel of sorts, it may focus on all-new characters or the surviving ones like Ghost and the Korean characters introduced in MW4. The film is due out in 2028, so we'll likely hear more on casting sometime next year as filming nears.

articles.summary: Farmer Needs Shelter is an Enshrouded quest that tasks you with providing shelter for your Farmer so they can operate to their full potential. If you're
articles.body:
Farmer Needs Shelter is an Enshrouded quest that tasks you with providing shelter for your Farmer so they can operate to their full potential. If you're wondering what exactly constitutes 'shelter' and how to create it, we've got everything you need to know in this Enshrouded guide.

So you've successfully completed the Growing Stronger Together quest and got yourself a Farmer to spice up your base. But the Farmer can't thrive without some shelter! The first thing you need to get started is some sort of room. You will probably already have a decent base going by the time you rescue the Farmer.

But if not, the lands are full of ruins in Enshrouded, and if you don't have enough materials to craft a base from scratch, those places offer excellent base opportunities. Many of them will only require a little patching up, and they are good to go! Rookmore and Long Keep are great first base options!

If you're making a base or house for the Farmer from scratch, your first stop should be the workbench. There, you can craft building materials that you can use to create walls, floors, windows, and doors for your structure. Then, equip your Construction Hammer and select a floor tile. Lay out a base in whatever shape feels good for you, then craft some walls to border it.

Place a roof on top to complete your building. It doesn't even need a door to count as shelter, although adding one is a good idea. Once your structure is complete, craft a bed to place in there. The most basic bed option is the Crude Mattress, which you can craft using the following materials:

4x Torn Cloth: Found by defeating enemies.

4x Plant Fiber: Gathered from bushes and shrubbery.

Place your bed inside the structure, then use your Summoning Staff to summon the Farmer to the area. Click on the bed to assign it to her and complete your quest!

articles.title: John Constantine Movie From Evil Dead Wrath Filmmaker is in Development at DC
articles.summary: John Constantine Movie From Evil Dead Wrath Filmmaker is in Development at DC
articles.body:
DC Studios has tapped Evil Dead Wrath writer-director Francis Galluppi to pen a John Constantine movie for the studio.

The news comes via Deadline in a report that suggests the project is still very early on in development. It's not known if Galluppi will be handling directorial duties in addition to his work on the script, and there's been no mention of any casting details at this time.

John Constantine is a comic book character created by writer Alan Moore and artists Steve Bissette and John Totleben, and is a working-class British detective who dabbles in the occult and magic.

Keanu Reeves famously played a version of the character in 2005's Constantine, and a sequel has been anticipated by fans for quite a number of years now. In late 2025, Reeves issued an update on Constantine 2 , telling Fandango that a new draft of the sequel's script had been completed and that it was going to be presented to DC Studios. However, there have been no updates since then, and it's not known whether Galluppi's new script is intended to serve as a sequel to Reeves' original, or if it will be a completely new take on the demon-dispatching detective.

Meanwhile, Galluppi's Evil Dead Wrath is currently scheduled for a theatrical release on April 7, 2028. It will be the seventh installment in the Evil Dead film series, and will serve as a prequel to 1981's The Evil Dead, with its story taking place in 1972. Galluppi developed and brought the story to franchise creator Sam Raimi and his team back in 2024, off the back of the up-and-coming American filmmaker earning critical acclaim for his debut feature, The Last Stop in Yuma County.

Around that time Raimi told Deadline that, "Francis Galluppi is a storyteller who knows when to keep us waiting in simmering tension and when to hit us with explosive violence. He is a director that shows uncommon control in his feature debut."

articles.title: Wall Tapestries - Enshrouded Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Wall Tapestry is an Enshrouded quest that sends you into the heart of the snowy mountains of the Albaneve Summits to recover two lost halves of a woven
articles.body:
Wall Tapestry is an Enshrouded quest that sends you into the heart of the snowy mountains of the Albaneve Summits to recover two lost halves of a woven tapestry. If you're struggling to trigger the quest or find the tapestry, you'll find everything you need in this Enshrouded guide .

The Wall Tapestry quest is given to you by an NPC named Gunther Galeforth , who you will rescue during the Escaping From the Quarry quest. Once you've successfully infiltrated the Balefire Garrison "Windward" , summon him to your base and speak to him to hear about the two lost tapestry pieces.

The first Wall Tapestry piece is hiding in a secret room within the Balefire Tower "1000 Miles" in the Albaneve Summits region. This can be found northwest of the Albaneve Summits Ancient Spire. Soar off the northwestern corner of the tower and follow the road to reach it.

Once you find the tower, you will be faced with a long, bridge-shaped building. Make your way onto the long bridge-like structure and keep your eyes on the right side of it. Eventually, you will spot a small staircase leading down to a doorway. Head down there to find a room containing a silver chest. Loot the chest and approach the left wall to find a secret entrance.

Interact with the fake wall to enter the secret room. There, you will find a torn tapestry on the wall. There is also a Starfall Legend lore page in the room. Collect that to further the The Greater Golden Twinflame Sword quest while you're at it!

The second piece of the lost tapestry is at the Small Watchtower , which is northwest of the Albaneve Summits Ancient Spire.

Soar across the broken bridge once you get there and run up the stairs until you spot a boarded up door on your right. Smash through the planks blocking the door and use a lockpick to enter the room. The tapestry piece is hanging on the wall on the left side of the bed.

With both pieces of the torn tapestry secured, head back to your base and open up the Carpenter's crafting menu. There, you will spot a new recipe called the Wall Tapestry Showcase. You need 4x Conifer Wood to craft it , which you can get by cutting down trees in the Albaneve Summits.

Craft the Wall Tapestry Showcase, mount it on a wall, and place both pieces of the tapestry inside it to reunite the artwork and complete the quest.

articles.summary: Anton Goodwin is an NPC in Enshrouded and he lost his prized Jester Hat somewhere along the line. In this quest, you'll be tasked with finding and
articles.body:
Anton Goodwin is an NPC in Enshrouded and he lost his prized Jester Hat somewhere along the line. In this quest , you'll be tasked with finding and recovering the fun hat. If you want to know how to trigger Anton Goodwin's Jester Hat or where to find the hat itself, we've got everything you need to know in this Enshrouded guide.

Anton Goodwin's Jester Hat is sitting in a chest inside a small settlement called New Cromville in the Albaneve Summits. This region is northwest of the Albaneve Ancient Spire, and has been completely swallowed up by the Shroud.

Most of the enshrouded areas in the Albaneve Summits are in deep valleys surrounded by mountains, and New Cromville is no different. To get there, fast travel to the Albaneve Ancient Summit and head northwest until you pass by the Event Honor Hall .

That's about the halfway point, so continue northwest from there, and eventually, you will find yourself on a massive cliff overlooking an enshrouded valley below. You will be able to spot some tower tops poking out from the Shroud. That's New Cromville.

Soar down there and reach the settlement entrance. Stand in front of the door and look up and to your right to spot a grapple point. Haul yourself up there and turn left immediately to find a long passage way. Go all the way to the end and turn around to spot another grapple point.

Walk forward to find a silver chest containing Anton Goodwin's Jester Hat and complete your quest. There is also a lore page on the right called All Preparations are Done , which gives you some more background information on the hat.

articles.title: Biggest Changes and Differences - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake isn’t a simple one-to-one remaster. Recreating this iconic adventure in a full-blown remake means there have
articles.body:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake isn’t a simple one-to-one remaster. Recreating this iconic adventure in a full-blown remake means there have been plenty of changes big and small to the overall experience. After going through the game ourselves, we’ve taken the time to catalog the biggest changes we’ve found.

Of course, there will be spoilers for the original Ocarina of Time in this video, as well as some spoilers for this remake as well! So let this be your courtesy spoiler warning to tune out now if you wish to discover many of these for yourself.

In the previous versions of the game, there were four Empty Bottles to find across Hyrule. Three as a child, and one as an Adult. Now, there’s a brand new fifth bottle, intended to be the new first one you come across, and can be obtained upon your very first visit to Hyrule Castle Town, by completing a short side-quest in the Potion Shop.

Another brand new item to be found in this remake is the Business Scrub Seed. This seed allows Link to instantly summon a Business Scrub, from which he can buy some items, such as a Red Potion, Five Deku Nuts, or Five Bombs. These can be helpful if you ever run out of items in a dungeon, for example. They’re generally found in dungeon treasure chests too, giving you the opportunity to shop within them. You may also find them in grottos.

The Items Menu is now divided into three sections. Items exclusively for Young Link in the upper left, exclusively for Adult Link in the upper right, and then items that both can use. Some items have also been moved to the Equipment Menu, such as the Lens of Truth and the Ocarina. These now get used via the D-Pad, rather than the primary item button. The Lens of Truth has also been redesigned as the Lenses of Truth, and are worn as a pair of goggles on Link’s head. Additionally, the quick-select menu on a single horizontal line is back from games like Tears of the Kingdom and Echoes of Wisdom, as a way to quickly change your active item, rather than having to open the pause menu repeatedly.

The original game had three wallets: the initial one holding 99 rupees, the Adult Wallet holding 200, and the Giant’s Wallet holding 500. But now, wallets have grown in size! The starting wallet in the game holds 200 rupees, the Adult’s Wallet holds 500 rupees, and the Giant’s Wallet now holds 1,000 rupees. This increase in wallet capacity is also directly complimented by the game giving more reason to spend your rupees, even making rupee donations a requirement when visiting the Great Fairies for the first time, much like in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom.

In previous versions, you could obtain a strange stone or shard of agony that would help indicate secrets hidden nearby. Now that grotto entrances are easier to spot, you’ll instead be able to gain the Echo Gem. This item can be equipped to alert you if a golden skulltula is lurking nearby, and will flash both on your HUD and link’s outfit when you get close.

The game’s inventory isn’t the only thing to get a major overhaul. You’ll now find maps of both the regions and Hyrule overall to be more comprehensive and easier to read. This includes the ability to see both how many heart pieces and golden skultullas you’ve uncovered in a given area, and also reveal icons on the map where you’ve claimed them. Other points of interest show up as well, such as icons for different shops, minigames, fairy fountains, and more.

It may go without saying, but this isn’t a simple HD remaster with a fresh coat of paint. This version of Ocarina of Time is a complete remake with a whole new artstyle. Everything looks very high fidelity, and much more detailed than any previous version of this game. There are new animations, flashy visuals, and a beautiful world to explore.

This version of the game has modern camera controls! You can use the right stick to spin the camera around, unlike the original or 3DS versions. Gyro controls can be used to aim certain weapons, like the 3DS version, but this time around these items are aimed in third person, placing the camera over Link’s shoulder, rather than in first person. You can even move while aiming the items this time around, too! The updated camera controls also mean locales like Hyrule Castle Town no longer have a fixed camera perspective, and can be explored with full camera controls.

This version of the game features voice acting for many of the cutscenes! Not every line of dialogue is voiced across the entire game, though many characters still make sounds. It’s comparable to Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, where certain cutscenes were fully voiced.

In the previous versions of Ocarina of Time, Link would automatically jump when approaching a ledge. Now, rather than that, he has a dedicated jump button, allowing Link to jump at any time.

Link also now has the ability to sprint. Rather than repeatedly rolling around everywhere, which you can still do, holding down the roll button now lets Link dash to move more quickly. And since there is no stamina system in this game, he can keep running for as long as you want! This also extends to the ability to rapidly leap quickly while climbing, or dashing forward while swimming, which can be rapidly spammed to reach your destination quickly.

Many areas of the game have received changes in their layouts and overall looks. While the general structures are the same, any muscle-memory for this game may leave you noticing the small differences. Lon Lon Ranch for example is now integrated within Hyrule Field, looking more like a ranch in the middle of the plains, rather than a large, tall structure with a separate loading zone. And thanks to the previously mentioned mechanical changes of jumping and sprinting, some puzzles in different areas have changed as well.

Getting the Kokiri Sword in Kokiri Forest for example, rather than being a puzzle about moving the camera with Z-targeting to see around corners, is now about teaching the player to time their jumps to reach the chest on an isolated platform.

Despite redesigning some of the geography, there are still some loading screens between major areas of the game, to preserve the feeling of the original game. But many loading zones were also removed. In addition to the previously mentioned Lon Lon Ranch, houses can now be entered as part of their overall areas, and not broken up by loading. The entirety of Hyrule Castle Town, including the entrance, market, and back alleys, buildings and shops, and even the Temple of Time, are all in one loading zone. Lake Hylia is also directly connected to Hyrule Field now, with no loading screen between the two!

Time no longer stands still when in towns and other specific locations. After your first meeting with Princess Zelda, day will turn to night and back to day even when in towns, villages, and more. The music even changes in many of these areas based on the time of day, meaning you’ll get to hear some awesome different arrangements of several iconic themes. This also means that you can follow NPC behaviors based on the time of day, as many will change what they're doing or where they spend their time as the day progresses.

The entire game has been rewritten, with many lines from the original game being updated and redone. Many NPCs now have more thought-out reactions to their surroundings and events of the game. Even The Great Deku Tree speaks more plainly than in the original. In fact, you may find Navi is less likely to constantly chime in on what to do next, giving other characters room to impart their wisdom. The first meeting between Link and Navi is written differently too, where in the original she says “can Hyrule’s destiny really depend on such a lazy boy?” when he’s slow to wake up, now she says “what could the Great Deku Tree want with this sleepyhead?” Beyond these changes, various characters now also have much more expanded dialogue trees. This is particularly noticeable in Hyrule Castle Town, such as when you ask the first guard by the entrance about the town, he has a lot more to say compared to the original game.

A brand new addition to this game is the Hall of Fallen Foes, a new area to look at various enemies found across Hyrule, as well as rematch the different bosses. Any main dungeon boss or miniboss can be rematched here, and the game tracks your best time. There’s a boss rush for all three of Child Link’s bosses, a boss rush for all of Adult Link’s dungeon bosses, and the “Trial of the Hero of Time” which only unlocks after beating the game. This Trial pits Link against every dungeon boss in the game in order, starting with only 6 hearts. Link has to spend rupees earned through the battle on items, upgrades, and weapons. Each of these boss rushes reward you with an owl statue trophy in Link’s house in Kokiri Forest!

The Threads of Time are a new addition to the game found in the menu, and are effectively the game’s quest log, keeping track of your quests and progress through the game, with some added pretty visual flair. You can even find this tapestry in Hyrule Castle! In the garden where you meet Princess Zelda for the first time, you can peer through the window at an angle to catch a far-away glimpse at the full tapestry. In the original game, this was where you could see the easter egg paintings of Mario characters from Super Mario 64. While that means this easter egg is no longer here in the remake of Ocarina of Time, it does play into the idea of destiny and prophecy, which the Zelda series is no stranger to.

The original Ocarina of Time featured hidden holes you could uncover leading to small grottos full of treasures. These areas have been redesigned in the remake, and can more easily be spotted by the small bombable stone circles in the ground, or strange plants that need a bit of wind to reveal their secrets.

Some structural and puzzle changes have been made to Ocarina of Time’s dungeons. The first door in the Forest Temple is locked – meaning you can’t leave without finding a key that a lot of players missed in the original. The Water Temple has two fewer keys, Inside Lord Jabbu Jabbu’s Belly’s hallways have been condensed into a central hub room, and other tweaks that alter the flow of these dungeons can be seen throughout the game.

If you step into the volcanic Death Mountain Crater without the proper gear equipped, Link’s tunic will catch on fire and you’ll start taking damage. This is a change from the original, where a timer would indicate how long he could survive the heat. Now, it’s more in line with Breath of the Wild’s systems and reactions.

Alternate Dialogue for Changing the Order!

Ocarina of Time is mostly linear, but there are a few things you can do out of order. One of those is acquiring the Lenses of Truth before you’re told they exist. If you grab them before completing the Water Temple, you’ll get a secret piece of dialogue. Sheik will tell you where to find this special item you need to beat the Shadow Temple, before realizing you already have them. Ocarina is always one step ahead.

In the original, you could get stranded in Hyrule Field overnight after the drawbridge into Castle Town shut to keep the monsters out. Now, the drawbridge remains open all the time, so you can come and go as you please. And, you can no longer climb the chains on the side of the drawbridge, which used to lead to a good amount of rupees.

You may notice bright, squiggly lines on walls throughout Hyrule. These are thoughts left behind by fairies that are a completely new addition in the remake. Playing the correct Ocarina song in front of them can fully heal Link, while some of the Fairy Thoughts are actually tied into two newly relocated Pieces of Heart.

articles.body:
This guide covers the Heart Piece locations in the The Legend Of Zelda Ocarina Of Time Remake. Just like the original game, there are a total of 36 Pieces of Heart, though several of the locations of these have changed. Every time you gather four Pieces of Heart you will get a Heart Container, which adds another Heart to your total Health bar.

Find all of the heart pieces to add nine Heart Containers to your total Health. The remaining Heart Containers come from beating bosses. Below, you'll find the complete list of all 36 Pieces of heart, which are numbered in addition to the region you can find them in -- some while you're in the child era, others in the adult era (and some in both).

One of the first Pieces of Heart that you can claim will come soon after you meet Princess Zelda for the first time, and return to Hyrule Field. Head south to Lon Lon Ranch, where there's a large field full of horses. From the large field, head to the large crumbled tower in the far southwest corner of the ranch and head inside. There's a storage area here with nine milk crates, and a large metal grate at the end. Pull out the closest crates to empty two spots in the middle column, and then pull back the crate in the middle against the wall. This will reveal a small gap you can crawl through.

On the other side you'll find your first Piece of Heart! For every four pieces you find, you'll earn a new Heart Container to add to your total health!

Another early Heart Piece is found in Kakariko Village, off to the northeast of Hyrule. Once there, you can head up the stairs to the left and climb to the roof of a building near a large wooden tower, where you can spot a man on another rooftop nearby who has something for you, but getting to him can be tricky.

Grab a nearby Cucco that's wandering around the path up to Death Mountain, and run over to the Windmill. From here, you can jump over the fence to the other side, where a ladder leads up to a hilltop behind the large windmill. When you grab the Cucco on top of the hill behind the Windmill, make sure to leap over to the roof of Granny's Potion Shop (the blue rooftop). Carefully move to the other side of the blue roof closer to the wooden tower, and you'll find the man lounging on the lower roof section. He'll be so happy someone's come to see him that he'll give you a Piece of Heart!

Piece of Heart 3 - Kakariko Village Graveyard

Beyond the village of Kakariko past the Windmill is the town's graveyard. By night, Dampe the Gravedigger will wander the grounds, and offer Dampe's Heart-Poundin' Grave-Diggin' Tour!

Request to play Dante's Grave-digging tour, and he'll reveal several dirt mounds all across the graveyard area. You can guide him to any of the dirt mounds and interact with them to pay Dampe 10 Rupees to dig in the spot. Whatever comes up is yours to keep... provided something is actually buried there. Sometimes you'll get a few Rupees, other times nothing at all, but keep at it until he detects something heavy and asks for another 5 Rupees to keep at it, as it contains his special prize: A Piece of Heart!

Piece of Heart 4 - Kakariko Village Graveyard

Finally, pull back the grave at the far southern edge of this same row below the royal tomb, and you'll find one more tomb to drop into. No enemies here, but a large Treasure Chest holds a Piece of Heart -- which should be the fourth one you've found to grant you an extra Heart Container!

When exploring Hyrule Castle Town, you'll run into a lady who's constantly doting on her little white dog named Richard. However, once you've opened up the gate leading to Death Mountain, you can return to the Castle Town to find out from her that Richard has gone missing, and you'll be tasked to find him amid all the other stray dogs that descend upon Castle Town in the evening.

To find Richard, head down the alleyway past the Bomchu Shop near where the lady and her dog live. Richard should appear around the back corner, not far from the Treasure Chest Shop (there are a few other white dogs in other parts of the alley, so you may grab the wrong one and need a do-over).

Interact with the dog to get it to follow you, then return to the lady. If it's the right dog, she'll be overjoyed and award you a Piece of Heart!

Once you reach Goron City, you'll be tasked to find a song to cheer up Darunia, which you can get by finding Saria in the Lost Wood's Sacred Grove. Once you have it, head back into the Lost Woods, and from the starting point, take a left. This leads to a small grove with a friendly Skull Kid playing on his flute. Step onto the smaller trunk, and play Saria's Song with him. Any friend of Saria's is a friend of his, and he'll reward this new bond with a new Piece of Heart for you!

Once Saria has given you the Fairy Ocarina, you can enter the Lost Woods atop Kokiri Forest. From the entrance to the wooded maze, follow the music right to the east. This next area has a lower pathway where two more Skull Kids are playing their instruments on large tree trunks. Join with them using your Ocarina, and they'll start a game of "follow the tune". You'll need to repeat a randomized tune of notes that build from 3-5, and if you can follow along, they'll pass you a Blue Rupee.

Try it again, and this time you'll have to follow the notes that build from 4-6. If you're having trouble as they hide which notes you need to memorize, look for the placement on the prompt to clue you in on which notes you need to remember. Complete this task, and you'll earn a Red Rupee worth 20.

Play their game one last time for a super hard version of following notes that build from 6 to 8. If you can keep following along, you'll earn the ultimate prize: a new Piece of Heart!

In Goron City, there's a large Goron-shaped pot in the middle of the city at its bottom level. After meeting Darunia, you can light the torches around the pot using a lit Deku Stick, and the pot will begin to spin.

Once you have the Bomb Bag from Dodongo Cavern, return to the spinning pot, and look for a plank that puts you close to the top of the pot. You'll want to toss a bomb into the spinning pot, ideally when the "Happy" face is facing you. The pot will spin wildly, and depending on the face it stops spinning on, you can earn different prizes. If it lands on the "Happy" face, you'll get a Piece of Heart!

Piece of Heart 9 - Death Mountain Crater

Once you're able to reach the summit of Death Mountain after completing Dodongo Cavern, there's two Pieces of Heart hiding in the extreme heat of the Death Mountain Crater. Be warned, after around 4 seconds, you'll start to take a quarter heart damage every second, so you'll need to move quickly.

From the entrance, quickly dash down the slope and then to the right between two large rocks, and look for some mesh along the ground leading to a wall you can climb down the face of the inner volcano. Just below these two mesh spots is a Piece of Heart hiding in an alcove (which will also reset the time it takes to start taking damage), just be sure to quickly leap back up the mesh after claiming it!

Piece of Heart 10 - Death Mountain Crater

Sprint down the slope from the entrance to the northwest to spot a low platform, near a broken bridge with a large grey rock in the way making it impossible to cross. What you can do from this side is find a Business Deku Scrub here -- of all places! He'll sell you another Piece of Heart for 100 Rupees. It's a steep price, but well worth it (and will reset the time until you start taking damage).

Once you're able to reach the summit of Death Mountain after completing Dodongo Cavern, you can climb up the Death Mountain Trail to reach the top. Here, you'll find Kaepora Gaebora the Owl. He'll offer to give you a ride down to Kakariko Village, which you should accept and enjoy the flight!

Kaepora Gaebora will drop you off on top of Impa's House of all places, but don't jump off just yet. Carefully move to the back of the rooftop, and look down for a small cow pen that's been hidden behind sealed gates. On the roof of the pen is a Piece of Heart that can't be accessed except from this roof, so hop down onto the lower roof of the cow pen and claim your prize!

If exploring the area as an adult, you can use your Hookshot gained from the Graveyard on the bright green vines to the left of Impa's House to get over the fence.

Once you've completed the Dodongo's Cavern dungeons and open up supply lines from the Gorons back to the townsfolk of Hyrule Castle Town, you'll have access to the Bombchu Bowling Alley near the center of town. For the cost of 10 Rupees, you can try your hand at navigating Bombchus into a target on a far wall, avoiding obstacles and banking them off walls to reach 3 goals with 10 Bombchus. It'll take a bit of practice and angling, but there are some wonderful prizes to earn as you unlock harder courses:

For the harder courses, we recommend looking for a way to angle the Bombchus off the wall at angles to reach the back, or look for the small gaps between obstacles to drive a straight path through threading anything in the way -- timing is crucial!

Once you have access to a bomb bag, you can begin to explore Zora River, and partway up the river path you may notice a Piece of Heart sitting on a high ledge with no way to reach it. Climb up the path leading further east, and look back where the river splits down to the southwest. There's also a high ledge at the back of the large island in the middle of the river. You can't swim up to it... but you can float to it.

Return back to the sealed gate by the start of the river and grab the lone Cucco. With all the enemies nearby defeated, you can safely escort it, throwing it over the last ledge before you climb up, and then use it to float down to the high platform, and use the vines to climb up to the top of the island.

Looking north, you can spot a high platform over the singing frogs that hold a Piece of Heart, but no way to reach it. Instead, head to the southern part of the island and across to a high ledge that hides a second Grotto entrance. In here, you'll find another Cucco. Grab the Cucco and take him with you as you exit the Grotto, and then cross to the narrow platform where a Sheikah Stone is. From here, leap down to the Heart Piece using the second Cucco to float across!

Once you have access to a bomb bag, you can begin to explore Zora River, and you'll find a Cucco wandering around on the other side of a sealed gate past a Bean Seller. Be sure to take the Cucco with you as you continue up the Zora River trail to where the entrance to Zora's Domain is. There are several crossing platforms here. On the other side, a high ledge overlooks a second Piece of Heart on a tiny platform to the northwest. Use that Cucco you held earlier to do one more floating jump across the falls to reach it.

Upon reaching Zora's Domain, there's a secret Piece of Heart you can reveal by solving a little puzzle. Head up to the Audience Chamber in front of King Zora, and look around, notin the two lit torches at the entrance to the audience chamber. You can use a Deku Stick and run down the steps to light torches along the way.

Keep running between torches and then stowing your stick before taking it out again as you head down to the bottom level, and follow a path behind the large waterfall to find two final braziers to light, which will reveal a Treasure Chest in the middle holding a Piece of Heart.

When in Lake Hylia, you can visit a small area across the water from the two scarecrows to find Lake Hylia's own Fishing Pond. It's here you can rent out a fishing rod and try your luck and land a big haul! The set-up is pretty straightforward: try to find a big-looking fish in the middle of the pod, cast your line near it, then gently pull back with ZR and wiggle your line to get its attention.

When it does, you'll need to alternate holding left or right -- whichever direction the fish is trying to flee in, until it gets tired and stops for a moment. When it does, hold down ZR and keep reeling in until it resumes its frantic escape. Keep it up, and the fish will be yours.

The owner is pretty good at judging the size at a distance, and if you bring him anything over 40cm, and you'll be awarded a Piece of Heart!

Though much of Gerudo Valley is inaccessible to Child Link, there are still two Pieces of Heart you can locate fairly early (or come back as an adult). Though the bridge gate is closed, there are sections of the valley wall you can jump to, and along the opposite side you can spy a large Treasure Chest. The gap is normally too big to cross, but there happens to be a Cucco nearby that you can grab and float across the valley to the other side. Open the Treasure Chest, and you'll find a Piece of Heart inside!

Though much of Gerudo Valley is inaccessible to Child Link, there are still two Pieces of Heart you can locate fairly early (or come back as an adult). Look for a Cucco wandering near the bridge, and use it to carefully float down to the large alcove at the bottom of the valley with the raging river below that feeds out to Lake Hylia. Jump off with the Cucco and slowly float down to a large alcove along the waterline.

Head up this large alcove path up north toward the giant waterfall. You'll find there's actually a path behind the waterfall, and you can climb it to reach another Piece of Heart!

Piece of Heart 19 - Kakariko Village Graveyard

When you're still Child Link, be sure to purchase some Magic Beans from the Bean Seller in Zora River. Then make your way back to the Graveyard behind Kakariko Village, and look for some soft soil by a dead tree on the north side of the graveyard, just below some raised ruins with a Piece of Heart just out of reach. When you return as an adult, the beans will have sprouted into a floating flower, and it will take you directly to the Piece of Heart!

Returning to the Kakariko Village Graveyard as an adult, you'll find a new grave by the magic bean plant, where Dampe the Grave-digger's spirit lies, and has built out a race course for you to run. Keep up with him to the finish, and he'll award you the Hookshot. Since you can't go back the way you came, use the Hookshot to zip to a far ledge, and take the passage up to the Windmill. You'll be able to jump across the windmill's moving parts to find a Piece of Heart on a high ledge!

Piece of Heart 21 - Kakariko Village Graveyard

After you've run Dampe's race in the Graveyard as Adult Link, you'll be able to revisit Dampe and try again. He'll offer a second wager after you've claimed the Hookshot - beat the race in under a minute, and he'll have a new reward for you. To win, keep an eye on the flames he shoots out, make sure to keep sprinting at all times, and memorize the route you need to take. If you're still having trouble, come back with the Longshot from the Water Temple to zip up the last staircase and shave off precious seconds, and you'll win a Piece of Heart.

To get this Piece of Heart, you need to first be diligent as Child Link in purchasing some Magic Beans and planting them in the right spots. Head to Lake Hylia, and plant some Magic Beans in a patch of soft soil just outside the Observatory. Return when you're an adult, and the beans will have sprouted into a magic floating plant. Let it take you all the way up to the top of the observatory, and climb up the ladder to find a Piece of Heart here.

There are two Pieces of Heart hiding in Hyrule Field, but both of them will require a bit of time traveling to reveal their secrets. If you look just to the east of Hyrule Castle Town's gate along the moat, you can find a cracked stone that you can bomb revealing a Grotto entrance. Inside is a peculiar Deku Business Scrub, who won't trade with you unless you know the password.

To get the password, you'll have to become Adult Link, and return to the Grotto entrance. Nearby on a tree, you can now find fairy writing which has the password. Unfortunately, as an adult, the Scrub has already sold his wares. Once you complete the Forest Temple, return to being Child Link, and use the password on the Scrub to buy his Piece of Heart for 100 Rupees!

There are two Pieces of Heart hiding in Hyrule Field, but both of them will require a bit of time traveling to reveal their secrets. If you travel toward the entrance to Gerudo Valley, look under a large rock outcropping and you'll find a small Treasure Chest. However, as a child, there seems to be no way to unlock it.

To find a way to unlock it, you'll need to become Adult Link. Return to inspect the Treasure Chest in the future to find fairy writing nearby, urging you specifically to take what's inside before someone else does. Unfortunately, someone else already has. After completing the Forest Temple, you can then return to being Child Link, and head back to find the Treasure Chest can now be opened to nab a Piece of Heart!

After using the Ocarina to learn the Song of Storms from the Windmill Man as Adult Link in Kakariko Village, return to the past. As Young Link, head to Zora River to speak with the frogs, and play the Song of Storms. They'll be delighted for the rainfall, and award you a Piece of Heart.

After you've played all six non-teleport songs for the group of frogs along Zora River (Zelda's Lullaby, Epona's Song, Saria's Song, Sun's Song, Song of Time and the Song of Storms), speak with the grop again to play a minigame with them. They'll ask you to play the right tune matching the fly hovering over each frog. Play the sequence quickly, and you can earn a Piece of Heart:

To get this Piece of Heart, you'll need to have done your job hunting down Gold Skulltulas across Hyrule. You can follow our guide to claim the tokens as you progress through the game, which should get you to the 50 mark around the time you complete the Forest Temple. Once you have at least 50 Gold Skulltula Tokens, return to the Cursed Spider House in Kakariko Village, and talk to the father to get your reward.

Piece of Heart 28 - Death Mountain Trail

To get this Piece of Heart, you need to first be diligent as Child Link in purchasing some Magic Beans and planting them in the right spots. Head up the Death Mountain Trail and look at the entrance to Dodongo Cavern for a patch of soft soil you can plant the seeds in. Return when you're an adult, and the beans will have sprouted into a magic floating plant. Let it take you all the way up to the top of a high ledge where a Piece of Heart has been taunting you.

Piece of Heart 29 - Death Mountain Crater

This Piece of Heart resides in the burning heart of Death Mountain, atop one of the large rocky pillars in the active volcano. To get this Piece of Heart, you need to first be diligent as Child Link in purchasing some Magic Beans and planting them in the right spots -- but you can't reach this spot until you unlock access to the Fire Temple as Adult Link. Once you do, return back to being Child Link and play the Bolero of Fire to warp outside the temple. Quickly plant the Magic Beans before you light on fire, and then warp back to the Temple of Time. Return as Adult Link, and you'll find a magic floating plant to take you up to the Piece of Heart.

This Piece of Heart can be found in the frozen remains of Zora Fountain, where Lord Jabu-Jabu used to reside. When you return as an adult, the entire area will have become an ice field. Carefully hop across the icebergs in the water to reach a Piece of Heart on the northeast corner of the frigid lake.

Requires: Iron Boots, Zora Tunic (Recommended)

This Piece of Heart can be found in the frozen remains of Zora Fountain, and once you have the Iron Boots from the nearby Ice Cavern, you can locate the Heart Piece. Simply equip the boots and dive down to the bottom of this lake to find it among a ring of Green Rupees. You'll start taking damage as you run out of air, so it's recommended to unfreeze King Zora first so you can breathe underwater with the Zora Tunic.

This Piece of Heart is offered by the scientist who lives in the Observatory at Lake Hylia, though you won't be able to claim this prize until you're an adult. He'll challenge you to reach the bottom of the pool in his lab, which requires you diving a total of 9 meters. To do this, you'll need to catch the biggest fish in the nearby Lake Hylia fishing pond as an adult, and get the Golden Scale as a reward. Then dive down into the pool and talk to the scientist to get your reward.

After learning the Song of Storms from the Windmill Man as an adult, and playing it for him as a child, you'll be able to access the mini-dungeon at the Bottom of the Well, where you can uncover the Lenses of Truth item to see the contents of chests before you open them. Use this by returning to Castle Town and playing the Treasure Chest game, using the Lenses to locate all the keys to the next room to claim your prize -- a Piece of Heart.

There are two Pieces of Heart that can be claimed in the Gerudo Fortress area, and while you don't need to get the Gerudo people on your side to claim this first one, it's recommended to do so to make reaching it easier.

From the northern rooftops, head south to climb up a crumbling slope to the top southeastern roofs before doubling back to the north. When you find a gap too large to cross, play the Scarecrow's Song to summon Pierre and hookshot across to him. Look just to the left, and you'll find a Treasure Chest holding a Piece of Heart.

There are two Pieces of Heart that can be claimed in the Gerudo Fortress area, and this one will require you first completing the area to earn back the trust of the Gerudo people, allowing you to explore the area. Once you can, summon Epona and travel to the archery course on the southeast part of town. You'll need to score over 750 Points by shooting both the pots and large targets to earn a Piece of Heart as your prize.

Piece of Heart 36 - Evil Desert Colossus

The last Piece of Heart can be found far out in the desert past the Gerudo Fortress, at the site of the Spirit Temple at the Evil Desert Colossus. Once you reach this spot as Adult Link, you'll be unable to travel very far, and Sheik will teach you a melody to warp here as Child Link. When you do, bring along some Magic Beans to plant in some soft soil, then return as Adult Link to ride the floating plant over a stone archway with the Piece of Heart on top.
