articles.title: All Gold Skulltula Locations - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Like the original N64 and 3DS version, Ocarina of Time Remake features 100 collectible Gold Skultula spiders hidden throughout Hyrule. Collecting them will
articles.body:
Like the original N64 and 3DS version, Ocarina of Time Remake features 100 collectible Gold Skultula spiders hidden throughout Hyrule. Collecting them will allow you to earn special rewards, including bigger wallets and heart pieces. Even if you think you've seen them all, you'll find that the Remake on Switch 2 includes locations that differ from their original locations. This page includes every Gold Skulltula location in the remake, in the order you can find them based on your progression through the story.

Below, you'll find the complete list of all 100 Gold Skulltulas, which are numbered in addition to the region you can find them in -- some while you're in the child era, others in the adult era (and some in both). While all Gold Skulltulas can be tricky to spot, there are a few ways they can be tracked:

Outside of dungeons, most Gold Skulltulas can only be found at night. You can tell where they will appear by looking for small golden spiderwebs in out of the way locations.

In outdoor areas, certain Gold Skulltulas can also be found in tall narrow trees that emit a soft glow. By rolling into one, you can force them to fall down.

Patches of soft soil that you can plant mysterious seeds in also hide Gold Skulltulas. To force them out, capture a Beetle in a bottle, and let it loose near soft soil.

Each main Dungeon contains 4-5 Gold Skulltulas.

The first Gold Skulltula you can find in the Great Deku Tree is located on the top Floor 3F of the dungeon, found in the room with the Compass. You'll need to step on the small stone switch to raise up three platforms in the middle of the room, but instead of cross, stick to the left side of the middle platform. Defeat the Skulltula blocking a high ledge, then jump up to find the Gold Skulltula against the wall at your height.

A second Gold Skultula that can be found in the Great Deku Tree dungeon, this one can be found as soon as you reach the top of the dungeon and jump down to create a hole to the basement by destroying the webbing in the center of the room. As you swim out of the pool of water, be sure to turn around. There's a large vine wall leading back up to the first floor in case you need to get back, but more importantly is a Gold Skultula. You can defeat it with your slingshot, and then climb up to retrieve the token.

A third Gold Skultula that can be found in the Great Deku Tree dungeon, this one can be found as soon as you reach the top of the dungeon and jump down to create a hole to the basement by destroying the webbing in the center of the room, and is located in the same area as the previous Gold Skultula.

As you drop down near the large dividing pool of water, check the northern side to find a large grate where a third Gold Skultula is hiding. You can shoot it from afar with your Slingshot, and then leap to the grate to claim the token.

The fourth and final Gold Skulltula found in the Great Deku Tree dungeon can be found in the basement B1 level along with two others. To reach it, you'll need to make your way through the passageways in the northwest, located west of the webbed hole leading down to the boss arena on B2.

The room the Gold Skultula is hiding in is the one where three Gohma Larva will fall down from the ceiling. Once defeated, note the webbing in the top northwest corner of the room. Use the nearby lit torch to light up a Deku Stick so you can burn the webbing away, and defeat the Deku Baba and regular Skulltula guarding the path to the final Gold Skultula of this dungeon. It's sitting high on some vines at the back of the room, and you can slingshot it before climbing up to get the token.

As soon as you enter Hyrule Field for the first time, there are already two Gold Skulltulas that you can track down, if you know where to look. One is hidden in a tree on the eastern side of Hyrule Field, not far from the entrance to the Kokiri Forest. Cross the small stream to reach it, and then roll into the tree, and a Gold Skulltula will fall out.

While the Hyrule Castle Town is a fairly busy area, you can actually find a Gold Skulltula hiding in the town as soon as you enter from Hyrule Field. Start by taking an immediate right into a room by the castle town gate, and you'll find an armory room littered with pots and crates, and one very bored guardsman. Roll into the large crates by the guard at the far end of the room to find one is hiding a Gold Skultula, which you can kill and claim its token.

Of the two Gold Skulltulas found in Hyrule Castle, one of them can be found immediately on your first time through the area. To reach it, you'll need to make your way past the initial group of guards by the front gate, which means climbing up and over the gatehouse, and jumping down into the gardens. From here, dart between the hedges by taking the middle path, and then hang around the outside to climb up the western wall to bypass the large locked gate. Look for a small enclosed area to the right of the vine wall leading up to the moat for some barrels and sacks, and a lone tall and narrow tree. Roll into it, and you'll dislodge a Gold Skulltula from its hiding place!

Of the three Gold Skulltulas found in Lon Lon Ranch, only one of them can be obtained during your first visit. As you enter the ranch, be sure to check around the northeast side of the ranch, behind the main house Talon is in. There's a small yard area with a wooden tower, and two trees. Roll into the tall and narrow tree, and you can dislodge a Gold Skulltula here!

There are several Gold Skulltula lurking around Kakariko Village due to the proximity to the Cursed Spider House. One such Gold Skulltula is hiding atop the main tall tree at the entrance to the village, where the Master Craftsman yells at his workers all day (and where his son slinks out to and rests at night). Roll into the tree to dislodge the spider and claim its token.

Gold Skulltula 10 - Kakariko Village (Night)

There are several Gold Skulltula lurking around Kakariko Village due to the proximity to the Cursed Spider House. One can actually be found by simply walking outside the Cursed Spider House and waiting for nightfall. A small golden spiderweb just to the left of the door is its hiding spot, where the Gold Skulltula will appear only at night!

Gold Skulltula 11 - Kakariko Village (Night)

Once night has fallen in Kakariko Village, inspect the building under construction on the south side of the village, near the Cucco Lady, and you'll find a Gold Skulltula on a high ledge of the red brick wall, and you can use the scaffolding to reach it.

Gold Skulltula 12 - Kakariko Village (Night)

Another Gold Skulltula similarly only appears at night in Kakariko Village, and can be found along the ladder of the tall wooden tower in the center of town, along the pathway up to the Gate to Death Mountain. Hit it with your slingshot and then climb up to retrieve the token.

Gold Skulltula 13 - Kakariko Village (Night)

Another Gold Skulltula in Kakariko Village is hiding out of view, and likewise only appears at night. To the south of the wooden tower and Potion Shop is another building where a little boy lives (usually out playing in the graveyard), and if you circle around the back of the house, you can find a Gold Skulltula in its web along the building wall.

Gold Skulltula 14 - Kakariko Village Graveyard

There are two Gold Skulltulas in the Graveyard beyond Kakariko Village, but one can be reached earlier than the other as a child. You can head up the steps on the left side to find a plot of soft soil on the other side of a small tree. Drop a Bug from your bottle (if you don't have one, look under the stones at the Graveyard entrance), and it will fish out a Gold Skulltula for you to defeat!

Once you've obtained an Empty Bottle and place a bug in it, return to Kokiri Forest. Look around the back of the Kokiri Shop, and you should be able to spot a patch of soft soil. Plant a bug in it, and a Gold Skulltula will jump out for you to slay.

Gold Skulltula 16 - Kokiri Forest (Night)

While you can't find this Gold Skulltula when your adventure first starts, you can return here after meeting Princess Zelda and the time of day begins to change from day to night. Use the Sun's Song (or sleep in Link's bed) to make sure it's nightfall in the forest, and then check around the back of the Home of the Know-It-All Brothers by the Training Grounds. It's here you'll find a new Skulltula hiding along the treehouse wall.

Upon entering the Lost Woods with a Bug in a bottle, take a left as soon as you enter. From this grove with the solitary Skull Kid, be sure to move south through a nearby tunnel. It will take you to a high ledge overlooking the bridge leading out of Kokiri Forest, and you can find some soft soil here. Drop a bug in, and out will pop another Gold Skulltula to defeat.

Upon entering the Lost Woods with a Bug in a bottle, take the path to where the shortcut to Goron City is. Head right to the pool of water, then left going north, and take another left. This will lead you to a smaller meadow teeming with several Business Scrubs. On the side near a large tree is some soft soil, which you can again drop a Bug into (one of the scrubs actually sells Bugs!) to reveal the last Gold Skulltula that you can get for now in this area.

Gold Skulltula 19 - Death Mountain Trail

Once you have obtained the Goron Bracelet from Daruina in Goron City, you'll be able to pick up and throw Bomb Flowers. Exit Goron City back onto the Death Mountain Trail. Head over to the Goron babysitting the lone Bomb Flower, and try grabbing it. You can then toss it over the ledge and down toward the large cracked boulder blocking the entrance to Dodongo Cavern, which will explode to reveal its entrance!

Note the patch of soft soil just inside the tunnel, and drop a Bug inside to scare out a Gold Skulltula that you can defeat for a token.

Near the end of the hallway is a shorter ledge, with three more Baby Dodongo that appear. Before you slice them, look to the right for a large cracked wall. Lure the Baby Dodongos over and defeat one when it's close to the wall, and it will explode like a bomb to break apart the wall, revealing a Gold Skulltula to defeat and grab its token!

One of several Gold Skulltulas that can be found in the Dodongo Cavern dungeon, this one can be found in the first hallway leading east from the main entrance hall with the giant skull. Near the back of the hall where three Baby Dodongos emerge is a large cracked wall. While there are no Bomb Flowers around, you can either lure the exploding enemies near the wall, or come back with bombs when you have them. Behind the cracked wall is a Gold Skulltula flanked by a few Keese waiting to ambush you.

One of several Gold Skulltulas that can be found in the Dodongo Cavern dungeon, this one can be found on the northwestern side of the first floor, off the main entrance room with the large skull, Make your way north to an area with a large raised staircase high above you. There are Bomb Flowers all around its base, with a small gap near the front. Look for a separate Bomb Flower away from the rest, and place it in the small gap so you can unleash one continuous explosion setting off all the bombs in a chain around the stairs.

This will erode the structure, causing it to sink into the ground, and make the large staircase accessible to climb up. Head up from the large stairs to the higher level on the south side of the room, but be sure to turn around before you reach the exit. There's a large mesh wall here, with a Gold Skulltula hanging from the side among some Skullwalltulas. Hit them with slingshots, then climb up the mesh to grab your token.

One of several Gold Skulltulas that can be found in the Dodongo Cavern dungeon, you can find this one on the second floor of the large entrance hall, just after acquiring a Bomb Bag and some Bombs. At the far northeast corner of this area by the giant skull, there's another cracked wall you can detonate with a bomb. This will reveal a room with two Dodongos pacing around a large rock in the middle of the room, and on the other side you'll find a Gold Skulltula hiding (which can be killed by a detonating Dodongo!).

One of several Gold Skulltulas that can be found in the Dodongo Cavern dungeon, you'll find this spider after you have unlocked the secret passage through the giant skull by dropping bombs in the eye sockets.

Head through to a room with several narrow pathways and stone blocks to push around and drop. After pushing the block down to the lower level, be sure and push the fallen block all the way to the far wall, where there's a ledge with a large cracked wall. Toss a bomb on top of the stone block to blast apart the wall, then climb up to find a small room. There are several Baby Dodongos waiting to ambush you, and near the back you'll find a Gold Skulltula hiding behind an Armos statue, which you can also toss a bomb at to detonate them both (or lure the Baby Dodongos into)!

Gold Skulltula 24 - Death Mountain Trail

After you have acquired the Bomb Bag from Dodongo Cavern, return to the start of the Death Mountain Trail. Just after rounding the corner from the path to Kakariko Village, look for a cracked stone wall by the Red Tektites. You can blow up the wall, and even if it's not nightfall, a Gold Skulltula can be found on the other side for you to defeat.

After getting the Bomb Bag, return to Goron City. On the entrance tier, head along to the upper left side and blast through the boulders to find a room full of brown and gray rocks, as well as strange black obelisks.

You can bomb a path through the cracked boulders heading right, then left, then straight to find two Treasure Chests with a Blue Rupee apiece, and a crate hiding a Gold Skulltula!

Gold Skulltula 26 - Death Mountain Crater

Once you're able to reach the summit of Death Mountain after completing Dodongo Cavern, there's a Gold Skulltula hiding in the extreme heat of the Death Mountain Crater. Be warned, after around 4 seconds, you'll start to take a quarter heart damage every second, so you'll need to move quickly.

Since you'll want to move quickly here, focus on running forward and look for two wooden crates by a pot on the left side. Roll into the furthest crate to find a Gold Skulltula hiding inside.

On the southern side of Hyrule Field, look for a large wooded area south of Lon Lon Ranch. Over by a large Peahat, there's a crack on the ground you can use a bomb on to reveal a Grotto. Inside the Grotto, you can find another Gold Skulltula to defeat.

Once you have a Bomb Bag from completing Dodongo's Cavern, you'll be able to head into the Zora River region south of Kakariko Village. You can then blow up the boulders blocking access along the river. This leads to a man selling Magic Beans, which can be planted in the soft soil you can also find Gold Skulltulas in. One such patch of soft soil is right next to the Bean Seller, and so you can lure out a Gold Skulltula here by dropping a Bug into the soil.

Once you have a Bomb Bag from completing Dodongo's Cavern, you'll be able to head into the Zora River region south of Kakariko Village. Head all the way up the river path to the hidden entrance to Zora's Domain behind a large waterfall. While inspecting the area around the falls, you can jump down at the base of the falls, and there's vines near a central platform to take you back up. Be sure to stick around this area at night, as a Gold Skulltula will appear around the backside of where the vines are for you to defeat.

One of several Gold Skulltulas that can be found in the Lake Hylia region to the south of Hyrule Field, you can find this one by the large observatory building. Outside, you can find a patch of soft soil, so be sure to send a Bug from a bottle in to scare up a Gold Skulltula.

One of several Gold Skulltulas that can be found in the Lake Hylia region to the south of Hyrule Field, this spider is in a location exclusive to the remake of Ocarina of Time, located at the far edge of the lake. From the large island with the huge tree and pedestal, start swimming for the far shores to the southwest.

Along the southern tip, look for the smallest of ledges you can climb up to find a tunnel entrance. You can shuffle through to the other side, where you'll find a Gold Skulltula.

After you've found the Empty Bottle in Lake Hylia with a note from Princess Ruto, you can show it to King Zora to be granted access to where Lord Jabu Jabu is at the Zora Fountain.

Off to the south, you can find a shallow path leading to a section of land with a few trees and a large cracked wall. Be sure to try rolling into the narrow tall trees here, and you can dislodge a Gold Skulltula!

Gold Skulltula 33 - Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly

One of the several Gold Skulltulas you can find within Jabu-Jabu's Belly, the dungeon atop Zora Fountain, you'll find this area soon after following Princess Ruto down to level B1, and taking the passage north. Located in this room, find a sunken area in the middle, you can step on the glowing switch in the middle to raise the water level here. Check out the vines leading up to a high ledge on the western side, where you'll find a few pots stashed away next to a Gold Skulltula!

Gold Skulltula 34 - Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly

One of the several Gold Skulltulas you can find within Jabu-Jabu's Belly, you'll need the Boomerang in order to obtain the spider's token. After you've defeated all the parasite tendrils blocking access to the two-tier room full of pits, jump down the blue-colored pit to a high ledge. From this ledge, first look to the north where some Biri float around to spot a Gold Skulltula along the wall. Using your Boomerang, you can now both hit it from a distance, and recover the Skull Token using your Boomerang!

Gold Skulltula 35 - Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly

One of the several Gold Skulltulas you can find within Jabu-Jabu's Belly, you'll need the Boomerang in order to obtain the spider's token. After you've defeated all the parasite tendrils blocking access to the two-tier room full of pits, jump down the blue-colored pit to a high ledge. Head down the hall toward the room to the northwest. This small corridor also has another Gold Skulltula hiding along the ceiling, which you can dislodge with your Boomerang and claim its token.

Gold Skulltula 36 - Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly

One of the several Gold Skulltulas you can find within Jabu-Jabu's Belly, you can find this spider in the final large room leading to the Boss arena. In this room with a sealed door and a very tall pillar with vines on the back side, look around to the backside of the tall pillar, and along the vines leading up to the top, you can find the last Gold Skulltula to claim in this dungeon with a shot from your Boomerang or Slingshot!

Gold Skulltula 37 - Zora Fountain (Night)

There's a Gold Skulltula hiding in the Zora Fountain, but it can only be obtained once you have access to the Boomerang from completing Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly. Upon returning to the fountain, be sure to play the Sun's Song here. Look for a nearby archway in the water you can climb up, and on the far wall, a Gold Skulltula will appear at night, and you can toss your Boomerang to collect its token.

Gold Skulltula 38 - Lon Lon Ranch (Night)

One of two Gold Skulltulas that you may have seen early in Lon Lon Ranch, these spiders can only be claimed once you have completed Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly atop Zora Fountain. Now armed with your Boomerang, check out the main house just by the racetrack entrance at night, and you can find a Gold Skulltula hiding on a window that you can defeat and grab its token with your Boomerang.

Gold Skulltula 39 - Lon Lon Ranch (Night)

One of two Gold Skulltulas that you may have seen early in Lon Lon Ranch, these spiders can only be claimed once you have completed Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly atop Zora Fountain. Enter the crumbling tower in the southwest corner of the ranch at night, the one that was hiding a Piece of Heart. Look up for a high ledge with vines you can't quite reach, but your Boomerang can reach the Gold Skulltula skittering around above and nab its token.

Gold Skulltula 40 - Kakariko Village Graveyard (Night)

Once you've obtained the Boomerang from Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly (or retrieved the Hookshot as an adult in the Kakariko Village's Graveyard, head back into the Graveyard at night. Look behind Dampe's cabin, and you'll find another Gold Skulltula waiting for you on a high wall. Now with your Boomerang, you'll be able to defeat it and claim its token.

Gold Skulltula 41 - Gerudo Valley (Night)

Though most of the region of Gerudo Valley is inaccessible to Child Link, there are a few Gold Skulltulas you can locate. Upon entering the Valley entrance, you'll approach a small wooden plank over a pool of water. Be sure to play the Sun's Song to turn day to night. Soon, a Golden Skulltula will emerge under the bridge, and you can hop down to defeat it and claim its token.

Though most of the region of Gerudo Valley is inaccessible to Child Link, there are a few Gold Skulltulas you can locate. Look around the bridge for a wandering Cucco, grab it and look down at the bottom of the valley with the raging river below that feeds out to Lake Hylia. Jump off with the Cucco and slowly float down to a large alcove along the waterline.

It's here you'll find a lone Gerudo tending to her cow, and nearby is a patch of soft soil you can drop a Bug in to make another Gold Skulltula pop out.

While there are several Gold Skulltulas you can find in Laky Hylia, one will require the Boomerang found in Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly. Head up to the Observatory and start walking across the rope bridge. Play the Sun's Song to turn day to night, and look back to spot a Gold Skulltula just out of reach, that you can now retrieve the token from with your Boomerang.

Gold Skulltula 44 - Kakariko Village (Night)

Returning to Kakariko Village once you are an adult, you'll be prompted to investigate the Graveyard and challenge Dampe's ghost to a race, earning the Hookshot as a reward. Return to the village when night falls, and look around the left side of Impa's old house for a clump of vines leading up to a high ledge. You can zip to them with the hookshot, allowing you to reach the stables behind with a cow, and a Gold Skulltula in hiding.

After you've claimed the Hookshot from beating Dampe's Ghost at a race in the Kakariko Village Graveyard, return to Hyrule Castle Town and dodge the Redeads that have overrun the plaza to reach what remains of Hyrule Castle. Now Ganon's Castle, there's not much left of the original castle, but you can find the old archway of the gatehouse. Look around the back side just over the large pit to find a Gold Skulltula hiding high up above, and nab its token with the Hookshot.

Gold Skulltula 46 - Kokiri Forest (Night)

Armed with the Hookshot gained from beating Dampe's Ghost Race, return to Kokiri Forest, and clear out the enemies who have moved in. Once night falls (or use the Sun's Song), head around to the back of the Twin's House (the one closest to the tunnel leading to the Great Deku Tree), and you can find a Gold Skulltula hiding high up at the top, and can be hit with the Hookshot.

When you're still Child Link, be sure to purchase some Magic Beans from the Bean Seller in Zora River. Then head to the Lost Woods entrance, and find a hidden grove by going right, left to the Goron City shortcut, left to the Zora River shortcut, left, and left again. Look for a patch of soft soil by a large tree to plant the beans in.

Return once you're an adult, and you can ride a floating plant up to a high ledge where a Gold Skulltula has been waiting for you.

In the large Sacred Grove area past the Lost Woods that leads to the Forest Temple, carefully advance through the narrow paths defeating the Moblins from behind until you reach the large stairway up. Instead, turn around to find an opening in the ruins leading to a Fairy Fountain, as well as a ladder shortcut leading to the top of the ruins you can jump over to quickly head back. As you jump back, check the eastern side near the roots of a large tree for a Gold Skulltula hanging to the high walls, and nab it with your Hookshot.

One of several Gold Skulltulas that can be found in the Forest Temple during the Adult Link timeline, you can find this spider immediately upon entering the temple. In the large entrance room, you'll need to climb a large tree full of vines to reach a key at the top. After climbing up, turn around to spot the Gold Skulltula at the very top of the tree vines to hit with your Hookshot.

One of several Gold Skulltulas that can be found in the Forest Temple during the Adult Link timeline, you can find this spider early on. As soon as you reach the main foyer of the Forest Temple where the Poe Sisters disappear with their torches, head directly north up the stairs toward a door with a green stained-glass window. At the top of the stairs, turn to the right toward a blue-tinted window, and you'll find the Gold Skulltula hanging onto the inside of the wall here.

One of several Gold Skulltulas that can be found in the Forest Temple during the Adult Link timeline, you can find this spider after you've defeated the first few Poe Sisters and claimed the Fairy Bow. Return to the third floor and shoot the eye above a door leading down a red twisting hallway to straighten the hall out. On the other side, grab the Boss Key and then look for a hole to drop down onto floor 1F. This path will take you out onto a balcony overlooking the northwest outdoor courtyard with the well entrance. Before exiting the balcony, carefully walk along the ledge to the south past a door, and around a corner to find a Gold Skulltula up here.

Requires: Hookshot. Fairy Bow, Scarecrow's Song

One of several Gold Skulltulas that can be found in the Forest Temple during the Adult Link timeline, you can find this spider after you've defeated the first few Poe Sisters and claimed the Fairy Bow. Once you have enough Small Keys, head up to the third floor and go down the twisting red hallway, through the Poe Sister Rooms and to the end of the straight blue hallway, where you can unfreeze an eye target to twist the blue hallway. This will open up a pit to drop back down to floor 1F, and the path here will lead you out onto a ledge above the northeast outdoor courtyard. You can push a block here for a shortcut, but if you look up above, you can spot some gusting wind. You'll need to play the Scarecrow's Song to summon Pierre, and then hookshot up to the high ledge using the scarecrow to find the Gold Skulltula up here.

One of several Gold Skulltulas that can be found in the Forest Temple during the Adult Link timeline, you can find this spider after you've defeated the all four Poe Sisters and unlocked the elevator to the basement. As soon as you arrive in B1, turn around and look for a small room to the south. It's guarded by a Skulltula, but after defeating it you can walk into the room and look to the right to find a Gold Skulltula as well. If the way is blocked, just keep pushing the handholds around to open the room to open up access to the southern alcove.

After you visit the Windmill as Adult Link and learn the Song of Storms from the crazed Windmill Man, you can use it to reveal certain grottos. Return to Child Link after completing the Forest Temple, and head back to Hyrule Castle. Evade the guards until you return to the spot where Malon was sleeping, and in the southeast corner by the tree you can find a strange plant with propeller-looking leaves. Play the Song of Storms to make the leaves spin and reveal a Grotto. Down below, bomb the cracked walls to locate a Gold Skulltula.

There's a tricky Gold Skulltula hiding in Hyrule Field, but the process to uncover it will involve a bit of time travel. Because of this, its easier to do after completing the Forest Temple, when you can freely swap between Child and Adult Era. As Child Link, head to the southeast part of Hyrule Field in a small wetland area with several large Peahats. Near one of the Peahats is a cracked stone on the ground you can bomb to reveal a Grotto. Inside, you can find fairy writing that urges you to destroy the regular Skullwalltula here.

After doing this, take the Master Sword and become Adult Link, and return to the Grotto. With the Skullwalltula gone, a Gold Skulltula will have taken its place.

There's only one Gold Skulltula hiding in an early dungeon you'll first explore a child, but can only claim the token as an adult. Once you've become Adult Link and gained the Hookshot, head to Lake Hylia to learn the Scarecrow's Song, and then head up the Death Mountain Trail to re-enter Dodongo Cavern. Take the pathway off the main entrance hall to the first hallway to the east where you encounter some Baby Dodongos. Nearby you'll find a high ledge with gusting wind, and you can play the Scarecrow's Song to summon Pierre. Hookshot up to him, and you can claim the Gold Skulltula token.

Upon returning to Goron City as Adult Link, you'll find a new Gold Skulltula hiding in the city when night falls outside. Drop down from the highest ring to one level below, and move around to the back of the high central platform that used to hold the Spiritual Stone of Fire. At the back of the rock jutting downward, you'll find a Gold Skulltula.

Gold Skulltula 58 - Death Mountain Crater

This Gold Skulltula resides in the burning heart of Death Mountain, but to reach it, you'll need to have gained access to the Fire Temple as Adult Link. Once you do, make sure you have a bottled Bug, and return back to being Child Link and play the Bolero of Fire to warp outside the temple. Quickly plant the bugs into the nearby soft soil to reveal a Gold Skulltula.

One of several Gold Skulltulas that are hiding within the Fire Temple, you can find this spider early on in your exploration. Soon after entering, head from the entrance hall to the eastern room, a large area filled with lava and moving platforms. Make your way to the top northeast corner of the room to find a high ledge with a large blue block you can use the Song of Time to move out of the way. Head through the door and fend of Flying Tiles and a Like Like to find a Gold Skulltula in the back of the room.

One of several Gold Skulltulas that are hiding within the Fire Temple, you can find this spider early on in your exploration. After creating a lift up to floor 3F, you'll enter a large room full of rolling boulders on the eastern side of the map. Hop down and avoid the boulders as you make your way along the walls to the north. Look for a cracked wall, and bomb it to reveal a Gold Skulltula.

One of several Gold Skulltulas that are hiding within the Fire Temple, this spider is one of two you can find after you've explored the large eastern room on 3F on both sides, and raced the fire wall to a high ledge leading back to the upper platforms of the room with the rolling boulders. Jump to the first platform and turn around to see a gust of wind on a high ledge above, and play the Scarecrow Song to reveal Pierre. Hookshot up to him, and look for a nearby platform to hookshot to, taking you up to floor 4F, at the top of the mesh walls by the door to floor 5F, you'll find a Gold Skulltula.

One of several Gold Skulltulas that are hiding within the Fire Temple, this spider is one of two you can find after you've explored the large eastern room on 3F on both sides, and raced the fire wall to a high ledge leading back to the upper platforms of the room with the rolling boulders. Jump to the first platform and turn around to see a gust of wind on a high ledge above, and play the Scarecrow Song to reveal Pierre. Hookshot up to him, and look for a nearby platform to hookshot to, taking you up to floor 5F. After you enter the large circular room, look along the inner wall over a lava pit to spot the Gold Skulltula.

One of several Gold Skulltulas that are hiding within the Fire Temple, you can find this spider after acquiring the Megaton Hammer within the dungeon. Once you have the special item, return to the entrance hall, and knock aside a statue blocking a door in the lower right corner. Follow the hall to a room with several Flying Tiles and a Like Like, and then destroy the large rock at the back of the room to reveal a Gold Skulltula.

Gold Skulltula 64 - Death Mountain Trail (Night)

After obtaining the Megaton Hammer from the Fire Temple, return to the Death Mountain Trail's summit by the Great Fairy Fountain. Head back down the trail path wall toward Goron City, and look for a large grey rock you can destroy with the hammer, revealing a Gold Skulltula at night.

Gold Skulltula 65 - Death Mountain Trail (Night)

After obtaining the Megaton Hammer from the Fire Temple, exit Goron City and look for a large grey rock by where the lone Bomb Flower used to be. Destroy the rock with the hammer, and at night you'll find a Gold Skulltula.

Head up the Zora River as Adult Link, and either use the floating magic plant from the beans you planted as a child, or use a Cucco to get to the top of the large island in the middle of the river. Along its south side, you can find a crossing to a high ledge, and near it, a Gold Skulltula will appear at night in range of your Hookshot.

Head up the Zora River as Adult Link, and make your way to the top of the river where the falls conceal the entrance to Zora's Domain. Look back to the west as you reach this area, and there will be a Gold Skulltula at night hanging from the high walls in range of your hookshot.

Upon entering Zora's Domain as an adult, you'll find the entire place has frozen, including the large waterfall. Just next to the waterfall and to the left of the stairs leading to the audience chamber is a Gold Skulltula, and you can head to the top of the frozen waterfall to reach it by aiming left from the ledge.

One of a few Gold Skulltulas that is hiding in the Ice Cavern mini-dungeon atop Zora Fountain. You can find this one in the first large room with a pair of spinning scythes where you need to collect 5 silver Rupees. Carefully move around the blades and look up at the southern wall to find the Gold Skulltula.

One of a few Gold Skulltulas that is hiding in the Ice Cavern mini-dungeon atop Zora Fountain. You can find this one after you find the first font of Blue Fire. Take a bottle and burn away the red ice above the room with the two spinning scythes to find a passage to the east. At the end of this hall, look behind a large icy pillar right next to the Treasure Chest with the Compass inside.

One of a few Gold Skulltulas that is hiding in the Ice Cavern mini-dungeon atop Zora Fountain. You can find this one after you find the first font of Blue Fire. Take a bottle and burn away the red ice blocking the path to the west in the room with the two spinning scythes. This leads to an area with a block-sliding puzzle, and once you jump across to the icy ground, look back the way you came to spot a Gold Skulltula on a low wall.

There's a Golden Skulltula hiding in the Observatory at Lake Hylia, though you won't be able to claim this prize until you're an adult. Once you've obtained the Iron Boots from the Ice Cavern above Zora Fountain, return to Lake Hylia and equip the boots to drop to the bottom of the pool in the lab. There's a crate down here (and a surprise!) and you can roll into it to reveal a Gold Skulltula, which you can defeat with your Hookshot.

Requires: Iron Boots, Zora Tunic, Hookshot

One of several Gold Skulltulas that hide in the puzzling Water Temple, you can find this one shortly after raising the water level up to floor 2F in the main central pillar building at the entrance. Once you have, return to the bottom floor of the pillar room to find an opening to the basement B1 now that a floating block has gone up. Hit a green switch with your Hookshot to reveal a hatch and climb up to find a Gold Skulltula.

One of several Gold Skulltulas that hide in the puzzling Water Temple, you can find this one shortly after raising the water level up to floor 2F in the main central pillar building at the entrance. Once you have, return to the eastern room on floor 1F, where you first met Princess Ruto, and float up to a ledge with a cracked wall. Destroy the wall with a bomb to find a room with several enemies, and a Gold Skulltula hiding in the corner.

Requires: Iron Boots, Zora Tunic, Longshot

One of several Gold Skulltulas that hide in the puzzling Water Temple, you can find this one shortly after gaining the Longshot by defeating Shadow Link. Once you have the Longshot, you can drop down into a long cavern with a raging river on floor 2F leading back to the main room. The cavern has many twists and is full of whirlpools, and once the path curves south, turn around and look up above the water for a Gold Skulltula on a high rocky outcropping you can reach with the Longshot while underwater.

One of several Gold Skulltulas that hide in the puzzling Water Temple, you can find this one shortly after gaining the Longshot by defeating Shadow Link. Once you have the Longshot, return to the central room with the tall pillar room when the water is down to the first level. Enter the base of the pillar room and work your way up to raise the level up one floor, then look upward for hookshot targets to reach the top of the room with, and you'll find a Gold Skulltula along the ceiling that can be reached with the Longshot.

One of several Gold Skulltulas that hide in the puzzling Water Temple, you can find this one just before reaching the Boss Key Chest. Once you have the Longshot, you can begin to explore the series of rooms in the north of the central room on Floor 1F. This will lead you to an area with narrow flooded paths that rolling boulders continually pass through. Look up at the middle pit the boulders fall down from to find a Gold Skulltula opposite the waterfall.

Once you have beaten the Water Temple and collected the Longshot, you'll return to the island in the middle of Lake Hylia with a giant tree on it. Turn day to night with the Sun's Song, and look for a patch of vines near the top of the tree you can reach with your Longshot, and the Gold Skulltula can be found at the top.

Requires: Song of Storms, Lenses of Truth

After learning the Song of Storms from the Windmill Man as an adult and playing it for him as a child, you can enter the mini-dungeon at the Bottom of the Well. We recommend completing it to find the Lenses of Truth first to avoid any pitfalls. In the main area with a long square pathway wrapping around a central room, head to the top northeast corner and use the Lenses to avoid a pitfall to enter a door here. Cross the invisible pits to the other side to find a room with a Like Like, and it guards a Gold Skulltula on the wall behind it.

In the Bottom of the Well mini-dungeon, there are two Gold Skulltulas each behind two locked doors. To find the first one, get the Lenses of Truth and return to the main area with the long walkways around a central square room, Head to the southeast corner and then turn toward the square room in the middle to find an opening with the Lenses that holds a Small Key. enter the large central room and make your way to the northeast corner to unlock the door to the Gold Skulltula past a pit with an invisible walkway.

In the Bottom of the Well mini-dungeon, there are two Gold Skulltulas each behind two locked doors. To find the second one, once you have lowered the water level, look along the west side of the main chamber for a hallway with a pit of water you can dive under to the other side, and burn the coffins in the next room to locate a Small Key. Return to the central room with the key and unlock the door in the northwest corner, where you'll find a Gold Skulltula guarded by a Deku Baba.

One of several Gold Skulltulas that can be found in the Shadow Temple once you've claimed the Lenses of Truth from the Bottom of the Well, you'll need to advance through the dungeon until reaching the basement floor B3. After crossing several platforms of falling guillotines and defeating a Stalfos, take a left to head east using the Hover Boots to cross a gap with invsible platforms. Defeat all the enemies in the next room with an invisible spinning scythe trap to unlock the far door where a Gold Skulltula is waiting.

One of several Gold Skulltulas that can be found in the Shadow Temple once you've claimed the Lenses of Truth from the Bottom of the Well, you'll need to advance through the dungeon until reaching the basement floor B3. After crossing several platforms of falling guillotines and defeating a Stalfos, take a right to head west to an area with five silver rupees that unlock a new door. In the next room, pull out a stone block and use it to get through the falling spike traps and then pull it to the far side to climb up. On the upper wall back the way you came, you can spot a Gold Skulltula.

One of several Gold Skulltulas that can be found in the Shadow Temple once you've claimed the Lenses of Truth from the Bottom of the Well, you'll need to advance through the dungeon until reaching the basement floor B3. Make your way around to the north by solving both silver rupee puzzles, until you reach a series of narrow corridors with wind statues pushing you back. When you reach a gap you'll need to cross with the Hover Boots before the wind starts up again, look instead down the pit to spy a Gold Skulltula just below you, and shoot it once you cross to the far side.

Requires: Lenses of Truth, Hover Boots, Scarecrow's Song

One of several Gold Skulltulas that can be found in the Shadow Temple once you've claimed the Lenses of Truth from the Bottom of the Well, you'll need to advance through the dungeon until reaching the basement floor B4. Upon reaching the area with the large docked skeletal ship, there's a large cage with a block you can pull out for a shortcut back to floor B1. Atop the cage, look for a gust of straw and play the Scarecrow's Song to summon Pierre. You can hookshot to him, and find the Gold Skulltula on a nearby wall.

Requires: Lenses of Truth, Hover Boots, Bombs

One of several Gold Skulltulas that can be found in the Shadow Temple once you've claimed the Lenses of Truth from the Bottom of the Well, you'll need to advance through the dungeon until reaching the basement floor B4. Ride the skeletal ship to the far western side of the dungeon, and then head through to a room full of invisible maze-like walls. Make your way to the far west room where three large spinning skulls are. Toss a bomb in each, and one will explode to reveal a Gold Skulltula inside.

Gold Skulltula 87 - Gerudo Valley (Night)

Once you've become Adult Link, there's a few Golden Skulltulas that will appear in Gerudo Valley. To reach it, you'll either need to gallop across the broken bridge with Epona, or gain access to the Longshot. However you do, look for the new carpenter's tent on the other side once it's nightfall, and you'll find some ruins behind it with a Gold Skulltula on the wall.

Gold Skulltula 88 - Gerudo Valley (Night)

Once you've become Adult Link, there's a few Golden Skulltulas that will appear in Gerudo Valley. To reach it, you'll either need to gallop across the broken bridge with Epona, or gain access to the Longshot. However you do, search the southern area opposite the carpenter's camp for a series of large rocks you can destroy with the Megaton Hammer. However, if you look upward on the inside of a natural stone arch, you'll find a Gold Skulltula here at night.

Gold Skulltula 89 - Gerudo Fortress (Night)

The guarded fortress of the Gerudo hides several Gold Skulltulas, and while its possible to find a few while evading capture, it's easier to get the Gerudo on your side first. Once you do, look for a fortress entrance up on a high level in the northeast, adorned with red fabric. On a high wall to the right of the doorway you can find a Gold Skulltula at night.

Gold Skulltula 90 - Gerudo Fortress (Night)

The guarded fortress of the Gerudo hides several Gold Skulltulas, and while its possible to find a few while evading capture, it's easier to get the Gerudo on your side first. Once you do, take Epona over to the horseback archery training course at night, and ride to the top northeast corner. Look around the back of the large target place high in the air, and you'll find a Gold Skulltula hiding here.

Gold Skulltula 91 - Mirage Desert (Night)

Past the guarded Gerudo Fortress, you can find a Gold Skulltula all the way out in the middle of the Mirage Desert. You'll need to carefully cross the line of quicksand, and then follow the markers until you reach a ruin to take shelter in. Look for a ladder down away from the sands, and in a small chamber you can find the Gold Skulltula.

Gold Skulltula 92 - Evil Desert Colossus (Night)

After you've crossed the Mirage Desert past Gerudo Fortress, you'll arrive at the Evil Desert Colossus where the Spirit Temple is. Use the Sun's Song to turn day to night, then check the northern cliffs of this area where some Guay gather in flocks, and you can also find a Gold Skulltula along the walls.

Gold Skulltula 93 - Evil Desert Colossus

After you've crossed the Mirage Desert past Gerudo Fortress, you'll arrive at the Evil Desert Colossus where the Spirit Temple is. Once you try to enter as Adult Link, you'll find that only Child Link can fit in a tunnel, prompting Sheik to teach you the melody to warp here. Return as Child Link and bring a bottled Bug with you. There's a patch of soft soil just by the entrance you can place the bug in to reveal the Gold Skulltula. (Be sure to also plant some Magic Beans so that you can get another Gold Skulltula later!)

Entering the Spirit Temple as Child Link, you can find a few Gold Skulltulas at this point in time. One can be found early on, after crawling through the tunnel to the northwest, and taking the door to the right. When you enter a room with a large mesh wall containing several Keese, there will also be a Gold Skulltula on the wall as well.

Entering the Spirit Temple as Child Link, you can find a few Gold Skulltulas at this point in time. One can be found early on, after you ascend to the floor 2F, and take the path east into a large room with a giant statue. Check the bottom right corner of the room by the statue's folded legs to find a Gold Skulltula hiding away.

Entering the Spirit Temple as Child Link, you can find a few Gold Skulltulas at this point in time. One can be found after ascending to the floor 3F in the room with the large statue, and taking the pathway to the southwest. This leads to a sunlight puzzle room with several Beamos. Head down into the corridor to the south leading to the colossus arms, and then turn around upon entering and look up to spot a Gold Skulltula here.

Gold Skulltula 97 - Evil Desert Colossus (Night)Gold Skulltula 97 - Evil Desert Colossus (Night)

After you've crossed the Mirage Desert past Gerudo Fortress, you'll arrive at the Evil Desert Colossus where the Spirit Temple is. Once you try to enter as Adult Link, you'll find that only Child Link can fit in a tunnel, prompting Sheik to teach you the melody to warp here. Return as Child Link and bring some Magic Beans with you. There's a patch of soft soil just by the entrance you can plant the beans in. Return as Adult Link and once night has fallen, ride the magic floating plant to a large raised plateau in the northeast, where a Gold Skulltula is hiding out of view.

Entering the Spirit Temple as Adult Link after you've solved the first part as Child Link, you can find a few Gold Skulltulas at this point in time. One can be found after opening the door from the entrance hall to the northeast, leading you to a half-pipe room filled with rolling boulders. Check along the left side past a blue block for an open alcove hiding a Gold Skulltula.

Requires: Silver Gauntlets, Longshot, Scarecrow's Song

Entering the Spirit Temple as Adult Link after you've solved the first part as Child Link, you can find a few Gold Skulltulas at this point in time. One can be found after reaching the floor 3F where the large statue is sitting. Head along the western side of the room to spot a gust of air over in the upper left corner. Play the Scarecrow Song to summon Pierre, and hookshot over to locate a Gold Skulltula.

Requires: Silver Gauntlets, Lenses of Truth

Once you've obtained the Silver Gauntlets from the Spirit Temple, there's a final few Gold Skulltulas to find that are hiding behind certain obstacles. Journey back to the Zora Fountain where Jabu-Jabu once was as an adult, and look near the Great Fairy's Fountain for a stack of obsidian rocks. Use the Silver Gauntlets to lift them out of the way to find a cave tunnel. You'll want the Lenses of Truth, as it's full of invisible Skulltulas that will block your path. Head all the way to the top, and turn around to find the Gold Skulltula.

articles.summary: There's a debate to be had about whether the Mosin-Nagant is better than the Oris 8.6. Well, both have their advantages and after spending several hours
articles.body:
There's a debate to be had about whether the Mosin-Nagant is better than the Oris 8.6 . Well, both have their advantages and after spending several hours with each, I've compile an aggressive quick-scoping build that will have you competing with the Oris 8.6 and other meta guns , like the M4 , ISO Nightshade , and VEL 46 .

So, which attachments does the Mosin-Nagant need to perform at its best? After spending several hours maxing out what many claim as the number one Marksman Rifle, I've compiled the best Mosin-Nagant loadout that will have you one-shotting your opponents with ease.

Mosin-Nagant Build Code: M03-3M8SX-6YL11

For this Mosin-Nagant build, I've focused heavily on increasing its range , mobility , and handling to create the ultimate quick scoping Marksman Rifle in MW4 .

It's important to clarify that the Mosin-Nagant does have the capability to one-shot enemies, but its success is dependent on distance. Shots taken at close to medium range will typically one-shot enemies if you hit the upper chest and head. For longer range shots, you will need to aim for headshots in order to earn those one-shot kills.

Here's our recommended best attachments for the Mosin Nagant:

To help aid aggressive plays and make quick-scoping viable, I've chosen the Schlager Visiv-5 Laser and No Stock to their boosts in sprint to fire speed, ADS speed, and movement speed.

Those attachments also help counter our long barrel selection, the Mosin K025 Barrel , which decreases ADS speed and mobility, but at the opportunity to increase our bullet velocity and damage range drastically. Without this boost, the Mosin would often struggle to one-shot in the longer range encounters.

To top off our aggressive build, I've chosen the TV-Light 7-Bolt for its improved firing rate and rechambering speed, as well as the 10 Round Mag which prevents us from having to reload as often.

Now, I will admit that this build might not be for everyone, especially if you're not a fan of tiny iron sights. I do highly recommend giving it a chance, because once you can master the sights on the Mosin-Nagant, it's a super satisfying kill.

If you'd prefer to use a dedicated sight, I would recommend switching the 10 Range Mag for an Optic of your choice - my go-to optics are either the SZ SRE-7, KV Corsac Holo, or the Cronen R808. But ultimately, you can select any Optic that you prefer.

How Does the Mosin-Nagant Compare with Other Marksman Rifles?

Well, for me, I'd give the slight edge to the Oris 8.6 as it generally felt more consistent and easier to handle. That said, the Mosin-Nagant isn't that far behind, and when you do get in a rhythm, it's a very satisfying gun to use. There's no real disadvantage to using either.

Perks: Quick Fix or Ghost, Blood Rush or Fast Hands, and Battle Hardened

Killstreaks: UAV, Counter UAV, Attack Helicopter

For your loadout, I highly recommend running a Semtex as your choice of Lethal, and either a Flash Grenade or a Shock Stick (once you've unlocked it at level 28) in Tactical. These are incredibly powerful, especially on smaller maps. If you're playing objective game modes like Domination , you can expect to rack up quite a few grenade kills each game.

Since I'm a more aggressive run-and-gun player, I'm running the following Perks:

Quick Fix for immediately triggering health regeneration when killing players or Ghost if you want to stay undetected by Enemy Callouts, UAVs, Portable Radars, and Heartbeat Sensors.

Battle Hardened , as tacticals are heavily used in MW4 and highly effective.

Killstreaks are more of a personal preference, but I've opted for UAV , Counter UAV , and the Attack Helicopter . These are particularly helpful if you're wanting to earn more XP each game.

articles.title: How to Farm Rupees Easily - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: In The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on the Nintendo Switch 2, rupees serve as the game’s main form of currency, and all players intending to
articles.body:
In The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on the Nintendo Switch 2, rupees serve as the game’s main form of currency, and all players intending to traverse the land of Hyrule will need them in order to obtain new armor parts, recovery items, magic beans, and weapon ammo over the course of their adventures. In this guide, we’ll demonstrate a few tips and tricks on how to obtain rupees easily and quickly so that you can spend less time farming and more time exploring!

For reference, different rupee colors represent different monetary values. The amounts for each can vary across each Zelda title, so for Ocarina of Time, each color provides the following amount of currency:

The ideal route for obtaining Rupees in as efficient of time as possible would be to perform the methods here in the following order:

Explore Hyrule Field, where you can fight Stalchildren and collect Poes along the way

Catch a few fish from Zora’s Domain, return to Castle Town to sell the fish

Play the Shooting Gallery minigame for any additional Rupees you may require.

Plan, optimize, and perform these tricks accordingly, and you’re bound to have enough income to max out even the biggest of the game’s wallets before you reach adulthood. Just… try not to spend all those Rupees in one place.

During your adventure, you have the ability to capture bugs and fish within bottles. While you will need specific creatures to earn specific collectibles, namely Gold Skulltulas for bugs and pieces of Heart for fish, you may always sell any excess creatures to a man in Castle Town. He’s located at the back of the town near a staircase, and he’ll reliably pay you 30 rupees for each fish sold. You can then repeat the pattern of catching fish and selling them to this man and swiftly garner a plentiful amount of rupees early in the game. Plus, you can get even more rupees more quickly if you have multiple bottles for fishing.

Castle Town provides another method for garnering money. There is a room full of pots and crates, and breaking each of the objects in the room will usually yield a few dozen rupees for the effort. You can then exit the room, and after some time, the pots will reappear, which you can then break again for additional Rupees. As such, you can simply wreck everything, gather the rupees, leave, explore Hyrule for a bit, and whenever you revisit Castle Town later on, enter again to easily get about 30-40 rupees per minute. The main upside of this Rupee-earning strategy is that you don't need any extra resources or even any gameplay skills. Just let loose and smash all the pottery!

The Shooting Gallery in Castle Town provides another method of obtaining Rupees that is more fun and simplistic. The only downside is that you’ll have to spend money to make money with this method. It costs 10 Rupees to play. If your aim is competent, you can easily clear this minigame and earn a payout of 30 Rupees. You can use the Gyro controls to make this minigame a breeze and thus earn a profit of 20 Rupees per minute. You can replay this minigame as actively as you’d like, so you don’t need to wait around for anything to respawn. Enjoy the minigame, and enjoy the payouts!

At night and while Link is still a child, Stalchildren will spawn in Hyrule Field. You can battle them and sometimes earn Rupees for your victories. The more Stalchildren you defeat, the larger they’ll appear. And if you defeat the larger ones, the rewards will be grander. You can get blue rupees for defeating some of the smaller ones, and you can sometimes get clusters of Red rupees for defeating the bigger ones. If you’re willing to fight these skeletons while the sun is down, then you’re sure to become extra wealthy once dawn arrives.

This is a finite method, yet it still bears many easily-obtainable rupees. After rescuing Epona from Lon Lon Ranch as Adult Link, you’ll have the option to go after Big Poes by jumping over glowing tree branches and fences in Hyrule Field. There are 10 Big Poes in total, and after catching each one’s soul and placing it into an empty bottle, you can sell them to the Poe Collector in Castle Town. He’ll buy them for 30 Rupees per Poe, and after selling the 10th one, he’ll give you 200 Rupees. For more information on acquiring all of Poes, we have a separate guide for that too.

articles.title: Nintendo’s designers strove for ‘elegance’ when remaking Ocarina of Time
articles.summary: An interview with Nintendo producers Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi about the launch of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Switch 2.
articles.body: The Ocarina of Time remake on the Switch 2 smashes together the past and present. The game retains much of the original N64 experience while updating it with modern graphics and gameplay that make it feel contemporary. But the mingling of time periods also extends to the development team. While Ocarina’s remake was led by producers Eiji Aonuma (a director on the original game who is now the franchise’s steward at Nintendo) and Hidemaro Fujibayashi (best known for directing Breath of the Wild and its sequel), the team also featured a number of younger developers, including some who had never played the original. According to Fujibayashi, those new voices provided some much-needed perspective that shaped the remake. “What really impressed me was the fact that they really embraced the theme of what not to change from the original,” Fujibayashi tells me ahead of Ocarina of Time’s launch when explaining the influence of the younger team members, who approached the project “very carefully.” He adds that “I feel confident that they weren’t necessarily pursuing something new for the sake of novelty when it might be unneeded and clutter the experience. They’re looking for elegance. Only what is needed, only what was important in the original, and how to carry that forward as their focus. And I think that’s a perspective they’ll be able to bring to future projects as well.” Much has changed since Ocarina of Time first debuted on the Nintendo 64 in 1998, and Aonuma has had the unique perspective of working on both iterations of the game. For him, the most obvious difference from then to now is the scope of the production. “We used to have maybe just one person designing the backgrounds, and that’s something that you couldn’t do nowadays,” he says. “A lot of the process is not so different compared to the N64 days, but the scale [is different]: There’s a lot more time involved, a lot more people involved, and because of that it can be harder to manage these teams.” [Image: What has also changed is the perspective of players. The original Ocarina of Time was Nintendo’s first stab at bringing The Legend of Zelda into three dimensions, and there are elements that can feel dated today; you can’t control the camera, for instance, or jump whenever you want. This feeling is only exacerbated by the fact that the most recent Zelda games have put a strong emphasis on player freedom. After building your own flying machine in Tears of the Kingdom, going back to the original Ocarina can feel restrictive. The team made a handful of changes, like giving players complete camera control and the ability to jump anywhere, which were designed to provide connective tissue between the remake and its present-day contemporaries. [Image: Eiji Aonuma. “When you’re developing a game like this with the free jump, we have to adjust the world to compensate for that freedom of the player,” Aonuma says. “I wasn’t quite sure about doing this in this title, but as soon as I felt it I thought, ‘Okay, this is a really good way to give players another way to approach a goal in the game.’ It adds just a little bit more freedom compared to the original Ocarina of Time. For me, bringing forward a little more freedom in this title is helpful because it carries something forward from Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom. Having that connection to the recent titles I think was really helpful.” The same could be said for the game’s overhauled graphics, which blend realism and fantasy art into a visual style that feels distinct from other Zelda adventures. Aonuma says the goal was to “bring out details of the world that people weren’t able to see in the original Ocarina of Time.” He adds that this was “something that we wanted to do in the original, but we didn’t have the technical compatibility at the time in terms of hardware output.” That said, the core gameplay of Ocarina still holds up remarkably well, particularly compared to other early 3D games. Fujibayashi was working at Capcom when the original launched in 1998, but he distinctly remembers anticipating how Nintendo would approach solving many of the problems that plagued early attempts at big 3D worlds. One of the most impactful features in Ocarina is something called Z-targeting, which lets the player lock on to an enemy, making combat much more intuitive. “The solutions are something that still stick with me as a foundation for when I create 3D games,” Fujibayashi says. [Image: For Aonuma, remaking Ocarina of Time was also an opportunity to address some issues he had with the original version of the game. For instance, one of the most infamous parts of the N64 Ocarina was Navi, a little fairy who serves as a guide for Link during his adventures. The problem was, in the process of trying to help the player, she could become overbearing and, in turn, something of a nuisance. While Navi is still ever-present in the remake, her chatter has been toned down quite a bit. “One of the things that we were thinking about in [the N64] development process is: How do we lead the player to the end of this adventure?” Aonuma recalls. “Can they follow along with the story? Something that we used was the Navi hints, and some of these were added just because we felt in that moment a palpable need for the player to have a little extra information. But it’s something that’s a hard balance to hit. You don’t want to give an answer outright to a player, you want a little bit of an information gap so that they have an opportunity to think for themselves and make that stretch. The more hints you add, the more Navi would talk, and that would change the player experience. [In the remake] we were looking for ways to make all of that more comfortable and more streamlined. And so using in-game text to chronicle your adventures up to that point, so people could remind themselves what they’ve done on the quest so far, helps us get people to the end goal.” [Image: Hidemaro Fujibayashi. But perhaps the biggest thing to address was the Water Temple, widely regarded as the most challenging dungeon in the original game. Even Fujibayashi tells me that he remembers it being “quite difficult” when he first played it. On the N64, players had to contend with an awkward camera and were forced to constantly open up a menu to use important items. But much of that has been modernized in the remake, making the dungeon less arduous, as players can now better see and navigate the underwater dungeon. “I think when people make comparisons from their memory now to the original version of the Water Temple they’re going to feel quite a difference,” Aonuma explains after I tell him I found the new version of the dungeon much easier. “So this is really nice to hear. As soon as you said that I thought, ‘We did it.’” Aonuma also felt it was important to keep Ocarina’s more traditional style of Zelda gameplay alive as the franchise celebrates its 40th anniversary this year. Breath of the Wild showed what could happen when you turned Hyrule into a true open world, Echoes of Wisdom took classic top-down gameplay and mixed it with an inventive new style of puzzle, and Ocarina offers something more straightforward. He believes that having all of those very different iterations on Zelda is part of the reason the franchise has had such staying power. “You need different approaches,” he says. And it’s those new developers, many of whom are fresh to Zelda, that he hopes will keep that philosophy going. “We’ve had opportunities to add to the playbook of Zelda, if you will, and the language of development,” he explains. “You get to see the progression of these ideas across the franchise. And now, working with younger staff on this remake, we’re having the opportunity to bring in additional new ideas. I really look forward to the future and what’s possible coming from the new staff.”

articles.summary: One of the most memorable details of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for many players is the presence of cuccos running amok across Kakariko Village.
articles.body:
One of the most memorable details of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for many players is the presence of cuccos running amok across Kakariko Village. They’re in boxes, in construction sites, stuck in seemingly inaccessible areas…basically everywhere. It’s all because of this woman Link only knows as the “Cucco Lady,” who has the most unfortunate job of tending to animals that she’s apparently allergic to.

Cuccos are still running wild across Kakariko Village in the Switch 2 remake of Ocarina of Time, and the Cucco Lady still can’t rescue her birds on her own. Thankfully, Link is a good samaritan, essentially the Hero of Side Quests. You can bring all of these cuccos back to their pen for her, and just like in the original game, your efforts will be rewarded with an Empty Bottle! On this page, we’ll show you exactly where to find all seven cuccos across Kakariko Village so you can earn your Empty Bottle!

There is no specific order you need to find them in, but this is what we did:

The first cucco is close by, in the construction site near the Cucco Lady herself, wandering around the scaffolding in the middle.

The second cucco is near the entrance to Kakariko Village itself, just by the gate.

The third cucco is inside a wooden crate near the center of town, on the side of the building where the lady cooking food for the village resides.

Before returning this cucco to the pen, bring it up to Impa’s house, and use it to glide down to the fourth cucco, which is found on top of the nearby pile of bricks.

The fifth cucco is found on the main path up towards Death Mountain Trail, heading north up the stairs past the tall wooden tower.

The next two cuccos are a bit harder to reach. Take any of the previous cuccos and bring it up to the windmill on the west side of town. Using the cucco you’re already holding, you can glide over this gap in the fence to reach the other side. Once over here, throw the cucco back over the fence so it doesn’t become stuck on this side. One of these Cuccos is on the other side, below the closed Potion House.

While you're here, be sure to look in for an open hole in the ground leading to a Grotto with a Treasure Chest holding 5 Rupees!

After tossing the last two Cuccos over the fence toward the well so you can collect them, climb up the nearby ladder to a hilltop behind the windmill, where you'll find the final Cucco.

When you grab the Cucco on top of the hill behind the Windmill, make sure to leap over to the roof of Granny's Potion Shop (which is sadly closed for the time being). Carefully move to the other side of the blue roof closer to the wooden tower, and you'll find a man lounging on the lower roof section. He'll be so happy someone's come to see him that he'll give you a Piece of Heart!

When you've returned all seven Cuccos to the Cucco Lady, she'll award you a new Empty Bottle to keep, giving you even more room to store milk, potions, and bugs!

articles.body:
Empty Bottles have always been one of the most useful items in any Zelda game as they let you store potions, fairies, bugs, and more! But actually getting the bottles isn’t always the most simple. Of course, Bottles are here in the Ocarina of Time Remake, and there’s even a brand new fifth one! So in this video guide, we’ll show you how to obtain all 5 bottles in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Switch 2!

The first bottle you can obtain here in the remake is actually the brand new bottle exclusive to this Switch 2 remake. Upon your first visit to Hyrule Castle Town, stop by the Potion Shop. There’s an old man outside who says there’s some sort of ruckus happening inside.

Speak to the Potion Shopkeeper, who reveals that a bug has escaped within the shop. He’ll give you an Empty Bottle specifically to find and catch the bug inside. This serves as a good little tutorial that you can keep bugs in bottles, so you can later drop them into some soft soil. Anyway, after catching the bug, the shopkeeper thanks you, and rewards you with a Red Potion…and you get to keep the bottle!

The second bottle can be obtained just after meeting Princess Zelda for the first time and returning to Hyrule Field. Head South to Lon Lon Ranch, and enter the house on the right-side of the map. Inside you’ll find Talon asleep once again, with a bunch of cuccos.

Speak to him, and he’ll challenge you to play the cucco-finding game, a minigame to find his three Super Cuccos in the flock. You get thirty seconds to pick up all three Super Cuccos, and the camera starts off fixed so you don’t really get to see where they go beyond the initial direction. Try to keep track of which cuccos you’ve already picked up as you scatter the flock. He’ll note when you pick up a Super Cucco.

Here’s a hint to find them: the three Super Cuccos have a different posture from the rest, and their walk cycle is slightly different. If you keep a close eye on them before they fly away, you might be able to spot them in the crowd. Successfully find all three, and Talon will reward you with a brand new bottle, filled with Lon Lon Milk!

The third bottle can also be obtained just after meeting Princess Zelda for the first time as Young Link. As you pass through Kakariko Village on your initial trip to Death Mountain, you can complete a side quest here to get the third bottle.

In the village, in the Southwest between the building under construction and Impa’s house, speak to the Cucco Lady, who reveals that all of her cuccos have escaped. If you find all seven of them scattered across the town, she’ll reward you with an Empty Bottle. With each cucco you find, bring them back to the pen and throw them inside to successfully collect them.

The lady will give you hints as to the general area of each cucco, but let’s go over exactly where to find them all. There isn’t a specific order you need to obtain them in, but this is what we did:

The first cucco is close by, in the construction site near the Cucco Lady herself, wandering around the scaffolding in the middle.

The second cucco is near the entrance to Kakariko Village itself, just by the gate.

The third cucco is inside a wooden crate near the center of town, on the side of the building where the lady cooking food for the village resides.

Before returning this cucco to the pen, bring it up to Impa’s house, and use it to glide down to the fourth cucco, which is found on top of the nearby pile of bricks.

The fifth cucco is found on the main path up towards Death Mountain Trail, heading north up the stairs past the tall wooden tower.

The next two cuccos are a bit harder to reach. Take any of the previous cuccos and bring it up to the windmill on the west side of town. Using the cucco you’re already holding, you can glide over this gap in the fence to reach the other side. Once over here, throw the cucco back over the fence so it doesn’t become stuck on this side. One of these Cuccos is on the other side, below the closed Potion House.

After tossing the last two Cuccos over the fence toward the well so you can collect them, climb up the nearby ladder to a hilltop behind the windmill, where you'll find the final Cucco.

When you grab the Cucco on top of the hill behind the Windmill, make sure to leap over to the roof of Granny's Potion Shop (which is sadly closed for the time being). Carefully move to the other side of the blue roof closer to the wooden tower, and you'll find a man lounging on the lower roof section. He'll be so happy someone's come to see him that he'll give you a Piece of Heart! Piece of Heart #2

When you've returned all seven Cuccos to the Cucco Lady, she'll award you a new Empty Bottle to keep, giving you even more room to store milk, potions, and bugs!

The fourth bottle is the only one that’s actually required to be able to complete the game, as you obtain it through story progression. You’ll need this bottle to catch a fish to be able to enter Jabu-Jabu’s Belly, rescue Princess Ruto, and obtain the Zora Sapphire.

When you first reach Zora’s Domain, participate in the Diving Lesson at the top of the waterfall. Dive in the water and collect all five scales that were thrown in to complete the minigame, earning you the Silver Scale, allowing Link to dive for longer. Once you have the Silver Scale, dive into this underwater tunnel, leading you to Lake Hylia.

Near this tunnel is a bottle, sunken down to the underwater ruins. You may see it glistening in the water at night. Dive down and collect the bottle, revealing that it has a letter inside from Princess Ruto. Bring the letter to King Zora, and he will let you keep the Empty Bottle!

The fifth and final bottle is the only one obtained as Adult Link, and it’s also the most complex of them all. You’ll have to find and catch 5 out of 10 Big Poes across Hyrule Field, and bring them to the Poe Collector in the Ghost Shop in the remains of Hyrule Castle Town.

If you speak to the Poe Collector and ask him about points, he reveals that he’ll give you something for catching poes if you earn 500 points. You earn 100 points per Big Poe brought to him.

You’ll have to approach these locations with Epona and your Fairy Bow, meaning you won’t be able to obtain this bottle until after you at least claim the item from the Forest Temple, and rescue Epona from Lon Lon Ranch. The spawn locations are long, horizontal objects that glow with an eerie purple light, getting brighter as you approach. Epona will have to leap over these obstacles in order to spawn the Big Poe, who then flees away from you.

A Poe needs to be shot with two arrows to be defeated. Once defeated, store them in an empty bottle. Once you have the Poes in bottles, bring them back to the Poe Collector in Castle Town. Sell him the Poes to earn your points. After selling 5 Big Poes, you’ll be rewarded with an Empty Bottle!

articles.body:
Throughout The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo Switch 2, you’re bound to collect all sorts of items, and it’s only a matter of time before you completely fill up your inventory. Fortunately, there are a number of upgrades that you can collect to expand your capacity. You’ll collect various upgrades over the course of your adventure, where some will be rewarded for completing main quests and others will be optional. In this guide, we’ll be showcasing how to obtain some of the earlier storage upgrades so that you may comfortably carry more items over the duration of your playthrough.

The overall amount of Deku Sticks you can carry can be upgraded twice in Ocarina of Time, and you can earn both upgrades fairly quickly. Each upgrade will bring you through The Lost Woods.

For the first upgrade, enter the Lost Woods from Kokiri Forest and immediately head to the left, past a Skull Kid playing on a stump, and through a tunnel to a spot overlooking the bridge leading to Hyrule Field.

On this path, by the bridge, you’ll discover a Business Scrub, who’ll attack you by firing Deku Nuts at you. Deflect the projectile using your Deku Shield, and it’ll soon surrender. You’ll then be able to purchase a Deku Stick capacity upgrade for 40 Rupees, which will increase your maximum inventory space from 10 to 20.

For the second upgrade, you’ll first need to borrow the Skull Mask from the Happy Mask Shop in Castle Town. Then, head over to Lost Woods and search for a meadow.

Hidden within it, you’ll be able to locate the hidden grotto full of Deku Scrubs. Equip the Skull Mask, and they’ll immediately swarm you with excitement. The leader of the Deku Scrubs will then offer you the capacity upgrade, free of charge. This upgrade will increase your inventory space further by another 10 spaces, allowing you to hold up to 30 total Deku Sticks.

In order to fire more Deku Seeds from your slingshot, you can track down these bag locations in any order you choose. One them requires you to play the Shooting Gallery minigame in Castle Town. If you win the game with a perfect score, your maximum capacity will be increased to carry 40 seeds.

If you did the minigame first, the second upgrade can be found in Lost Woods. Locate the hanging target (most easily found by entering the Lost Woods from Kokiri Forest and making an immediate right turn), and shoot the center three times in a row. Upon doing so, a Deku Scrub will appear and reward you with another upgrade, further increasing your capacity to 50 seeds.
