articles.title: Kokiri Forest Walkthrough - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains
articles.body:
Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains the same, there's plenty of new differences to be found while exploring Hyrule. This walkthrough covers the opening prologue of the game as a young child of the forest named Link is called to adventure.

The story begins with a dream: A child stands before a great castle. A young girl flees past, only to be followed by an imposing man atop a black steed. Elsewhere, the Great Deku Tree that watches over the forest summons a fairy named Navi, and requests that she bring the "child" to meet with him. That child is Link, who is about to take their first steps toward a grand adventure. After Navi wakes Link up from their strange dream, you'll finally be in control. Leave Link's treehouse by heading to the door and pressing the A button.

As Link steps out to view their home of Kokiri Forest, another of the forest children (called Kokiri) named Saria will come running up to call Link over. In the Ocarina of Time Remake, you'll be able to make full use of the free camera by using the right control stick, so be sure to get a good view of the area before heading down the ladder, and speaking to Saria by pressing the A button.

She'll be overjoyed that Link has finally found a fairy companion, and will urge you to head over the Great Deku Tree right away, so don't delay! You can find the entrance to his grove just down the road past a large cave by the water. As you reach the water's edge, you'll find that the Ocarina of Time Remake includes a new feature - a dedicated jump button! Try it out by pressing the X button to leap across the stone platforms to stay dry (if you fall in, just swim to the other side and Link will automatically climb out). However, before you can meet with the Great Deku Tree, a surly Kokiri named Mido will block your path. He's not entirely convinced Link has what it takes to meet with the Great Deku Tree, fairy companion or not. At the very least, you should have the right gear equipped first, like a Sword and Shield.

The first piece of gear you'll need is something to defend yourself with. Luckily, you don't have to look far. Jump back across the water but stick to the right side this time to find a tree house with a Kokiri girl sitting atop the entrance. She'll teach you how to target distant objects by holding ZL. Navi will fly over to the target, allowing you to interact by pressing A, just as if it was right in front of you! Head into the Kokiri Shop and speak with the shopkeeper. He's low on supplies, but he does have a Kokiri Shield in stock. However, he's not giving it away for free, and you'll need to pick up 40 Rupees if you want to buy it. The good news is that the forest is teeming with hidden treasure, if you know where to look:

Get started by looking in the corner alcove of the shop to find a Blue Rupee - worth 5 Rupees!

Next, head across the water and look below a small waterfall to spot another shimmering Blue Rupee in the water. Swim over to it and hold A to dive under for a few short seconds and grab it.

Over to the south of the entrance to the Great Deku Tree, you can enter the House of the Twins to find a girl singing about the different colors of Rupees and their worth. Just outside, look for some small red pots to pick up by pressing A and toss with ZR to find another Blue Rupee.

Heading west from the Kokiri Shop, you can reach the other side of the stream with more rocks to jump over, and you can find one Blue Rupee on a rock, and another in the water just below.

Just past the water, you'll find Mido's House with another Kokiri struggling to lift rocks (which you can help with to find more items). Inside, Mido has helpfully left several Treasure Chests you can open to help yourself to a total of 16 Rupees. I'm sure he won't mind!

Rupees found out in the open or in chests only appear once, but any found in plants, rocks, pots, or from defeating enemies can always be uncovered when you return to the area!

Once you have the funds, return to the Kokiri Shop and purchase the Deku Shield! You can also buy some Deku Sticks and Nuts if you want, but you'll be able to find them through other means soon enough. You can also talk to the girl in the shop who will give you some pointers about raising your shield when targeting enemies while holding ZL.

Now that you can properly defend yourself, you'll also need a way to defeat threats, which means getting yourself a sword. If you talk to the kid outside Mido's House in the northwest, he'll point you toward the Training Grounds up the hill to the south across from the house.

While you're up here, you should also check out the House of the Three Brothers nearby to learn some important tips about the menu, map, and using items like Deku Sticks and Deku Nuts.

Enter the training grounds and speak with the Kokiri boy to get a crash course in moving while targeting enemies. Using the scarecrow dummies, try out strafing, hopping, and backflipping all while targeting your "opponent". Do this, and he will reveal the secret location of the Kokiri Sword, which happens to be right through a nearby tunnel. Head to the wall and press A near the tunnel entrance to crawl down through to the other side. Here you'll find the "Kokiri Trial" which will task you with getting past the hazards to claim your prize. The hazard takes the form of a large rolling rock, traveling in the counter-clockwise circle around a tall central platform with a chest on top. Once the large rock rolls past, sprint after it by rolling with A and then holding down A to move quickly. There are a few extra Blue Rupees hiding in alcoves you can use to safely catch your breath until the rock rolls past again. Make your way to the south side, and you'll find a ladder leading up to a higher platform.

From here, you'll be able to double back and jump across to the central platform by pressing X, and you'll reach a large Treasure Chest holding the Kokiri Sword!

With the sword in hand, Link can now fend off threats with a swipe by pressing the X button -- but that's not all it's good for. You'll find that Link makes a pretty decent gardener, and you can use the sword to cut away nearby bushes and tall grass with his new sword, and can often reveal items like Green Rupees, Hearts, and other items. If you haven't already purchased the shield, consider grabbing any extra needed funds by cutting the grass! Hop down after the boulder passes and crawl back through the tunnel back to the Training Grounds. the Kokiri boy here will be excited at your new find, and offer to teach you his ultimate move: The Jump Attack. When targeting a foe with ZL, you can press X to jump, and then Y to attack in midair to perform this mighty move, which deals double the damage of a normal swing.

Beyond this special move, it's worth noting that Link can perform sword swings that can slash left or right depending on which direction your strafing while attacking, and can also make forward stab thrusts if you swing while moving toward your target.

Just like in other Zelda games, Link can also perform his famous Spin Attack by holding the attack button down (which you can even do after an initial swing) and then release the A button after a brief delay where he holds his sword back, to damage foes all around him -- though currently your range is fairly short.

Now that Link is properly geared out to face any threats you may come across, head back to Mido and show off your new goods to leave him speechless, and he'll reluctantly step aside to allow you audience with the Great Deku Tree. As you head through the tunnel, you'll encounter your first real enemy: A Deku Baba. This angry plant will shoot straight up, but thankfully leaves itself very vulnerable to attack, though it can wobble around and damage you if you draw too close for an extended period. Target it with ZL, then slash with your sword to cut its stem, and you'll be awarded with the Deku Stick! These items can be used as breakable weapons in a pinch, but can also help light up areas by transferring fire between torches.

Take out the other two Deku Babas blocking the way forward, and at last you'll have your audience with the Great Deku Tree. It seems your adventure will be leading you to some unexpected places, including Beneath the Deku Tree itself!

Up Next: Great Deku Tree Dungeon Walkthrough

articles.title: Great Deku Tree Dungeon Walkthrough - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains
articles.body:
Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains the same, there's plenty of new differences to be found while exploring Hyrule. After exploring the Kokiri Forest to equip both a sword and shield, the young child Link will now face his first true test: Defeating the monster that lurks Beneath the Great Deku Tree.

Now that Link is properly outfitted for adventure, you'll be able to finally meet with the Great Deku Tree, who has a task for this child of legend. Deep within the Deku Tree lies the Spiritual Stone of the Forest, which is vital to ensuring the peace of the realm. However, a certain evil figure seeks this stone, and has attempted to steal the stone by unleashing a monster inside the Deku Tree. Together with Navi the fairy, it will be up to you to descend into the mammoth tree and defeat the evil within.

Entering through the tree's open mouth, you'll find yourself in your first dungeon. These realms are full of secrets and puzzles, and it will be up to you to find a way deeper into the roots of this area. To do so, you'll need to be on the lookout for vital tools to help you, namely: a Dungeon Map, a Compass, Keys to open locked doors, and a Special Item unique to the dungeon that is vital for solving its puzzles.

As you enter the dungeon, the first thing you're likely to notice is a large spiderweb encompassing the center of the room. There seems to be a pathway far below, but you'll need to find a way to get through the tough webbing, which means climbing higher.

All around the webbing are more Deku Baba that will spring out of the weeds and bushes. Many of these will lunge toward you, rather than springing straight up like the ones you encountered on the way to the Great Deku Tree. Avoid their root-like tongue and step back out of their range, then retaliate with a few quick stabs (you can also block, but it will respond by readying up for another lunge, whereas sidestepping will leave it open to attack). If you strike and defeat a Deku Baba's head, you'll earn yourself a Deku Nut, while striking at the enemy's stalks will award you Deku Sticks.

Deku Nuts don't deal much damage, but they can be used to briefly stun enemies around you, making it a useful tool to have at the ready. You can do so by holding the R button and moving between equippable items, or equipping it directly through your main menu's inventory screen. With the first floor cleared, look around for some bright green vines, which you can jump onto to begin climbing up to a higher level. There's a ledge here overlooking the webbed pit, but jumping down from this height just isn't enough. You'll need to go further.

Head along the second floor pathway until you come to more vines, only these are guarded by Skullwalltulas. They can move surprisingly fast along the vines to hit you while you're climbing and defenseless, which means you'll need a way to deal with them. For now, focus your attention on the large Treasure Chest at the base of the vines, and open it to reveal this area's Dungeon Map!

With this map, you'll now have a rough outline of the entire dungeon, allowing to view all the floors and rooms, but their contents won't reveal themselves until you explore them yourself. Still, it seems there's a much larger area in the basement, which is where you'll need to get to.

Keep moving to the far side of the second floor to find a door into a new narrow room. The door will seal behind you, and can only be opened after defeating the foes in this room: A Deku Scrub. These guys like to burrow into the leaves where they can't be hit, and will emerge only when you're at a distance to spit nuts at you. Wait patiently with your shield out, and the nut will bounce right back to him.

Stunned, he'll begin to flee, allowing you to give chase, and once he runs out of breath, you can slice to get him to give up, and the door will open after he reveals a tip about rolling after a fall.

The next room features a wooden bridge leading to a high platform, only for the bridge to crumble as you begin to cross. Race to the other side, where you'll find a Treasure Chest holding your first big upgrade, the Fairy Slingshot!

With this tool, you'll now be able to take out enemies at range by using Deku Seeds as ammo for your newfound slingshot. You can either hold ZL to target an object and snap to it before holding ZR to aim your slingshot, or free aim and use either your control stick or gyro controls for more precise movements.

Try it out on the small vine wall to the side of the chest where a lone Skullwalltula sits, and then climb up to find a hidden Treasure Chest holding 3 Deku Nuts.

With the wooden bridge collapsed, you'll need a new way across. Look above the doorway, and you can spot a strange eye embedded in the wall. Hit it with your slingshot to close the eye, and the mechanism will release a ladder for you to climb up and go back to the central room.

Armed with your slingshot, approach the large vine wall and take aim at the three Skullwalltulas guarding the vines. Once they are dealt with, you can begin the climb (and rapidly ascend by tapping the jump button).

Now on the third floor, leap sideways along the vines to find a platform to drop down onto, and you'll find a long circular pathway high above the webbing blocking the basement access below. Before that however, look for the first door on the left, but be prepared to deal with a bigger type of spider. This Skulltula will block the doorway, and trying to attack its hard skull shell will have no effect. What it will do is cause the spider to spin (which you should back away from or risk getting hit), and then wait for its underbelly to show, and strike quickly. Two hits (or one jump attack) will be enough to defeat it, and then you can head through the door.

This room holds another Treasure Chest on the far side of the room, but the ground in the middle is too low to climb up. Instead, look for a small stone button on the right side to step on, and it will cause three platforms to rise up in the middle.

The platforms will soon begin to sink back down, so waste no time in jumping across to the far side -- but be ready for a Deku Baba to ambush you when you get there. Defeat it, and then open the Treasure Chest to claim your final major prize, the dungeon's Compass!

With this tool, you can now get a more detailed view of the Dungeon, and spot the location of other treasure chests, locked doors, and even the Boss location.

Take a look at the map, and you'll notice there's one such Treasure Chest on your map just a few feet away from where you got the Compass. Look behind the chest and cut away the grass to reveal a small tunnel to crawl through. Climb up the vines on the other side, and you'll find a Treasure Chest with Three Deku Nuts!

Returning back across the sunken pit in the middle of the room, look for a high ledge on the side with something gold and shiny. The path to the ledge is guarded by another Skulltula, which you should take your time defeating while still in the sunken area, before going back to raise the platforms by stepping on the stone switch again.

Hop across to the left, and you'll find a curious Gold Skultula. These creatures can't be targeted with ZL, and are hidden all across Hyrule in hard to spot places. Defeating one will earn you one of 100 Skulltula Tokens, which you can exchage for rewards later on!

With compass in hand, return to the top of the central room and continue making your way up. There's another Skulltula lurking above, and guarding a few Recovery Hearts if you need to get some health back.

Defeat one more Skultula along the narrow walkway, and you'll at last be at the very top of the dungeon. It's a long way down, but that's exactly where you want to go. Give a mighty leap into the center of the room and fall all the way down onto the webbing, which will finally give way and drop you down into the basement of the dungeon.

As you swim out of the pool of water, be sure to turn around. There's a large vine wall leading back up to the first floor in case you need to get back, but more importantly is a Gold Skultula. You can defeat it with your slingshot, and then climb up to retrieve the token.

In this first large basement room, you'll be overlooking a section of water dividing the room into two parts, and the water currently prevents you from reaching the back half of the room. Down below to the north and south are two large alcoves covered in more webbing.

As you drop down near the large dividing pool of water, check the northern side to find a large grate where a third Gold Skultula is hiding. You can shoot it from afar with your Slingshot, and then leap to the grate to claim the token.

Near the Gold Skulltula is a large webbing blocking a small Treasure Chest, but you can step on a stone switch to light the nearby torch, which will burn away the webbing, granting you access to Three Deku Sticks!

Take one of those Deku Sticks and equip it, and then stand next to the newly lit torch to light up your stick. Quickly race along the platforms to the south end where the other webbing blocks a doorway, and burn it away with the stick before it burns up in your hand (be sure to unequip it by pressing B after the webbing burns).

In this next room, defeat another Deku Scrub by bouncing the incoming nut back to its face, and it will reveal a secret about some of its friends blocking the way up ahead. You can unlock the far door in this room by hitting the eye symbol above the door with your slingshot.

This room features a large pool of water with a platforming floating between both ends. However, the platform floats right under a large spinning axle covered in thorns, making it impossible to duck under.

To solve this puzzle, leap into the water and look to the left below a large grate to find a switch on the floor. Dive down to hit it, and a large block will suck some of the water in the room, lowering the floating platform so that you'll have enough room to ride it under the thorns to the far side.

A lone Skulltula guards a high ledge beyond this room, and after defeating it you'll find it's too high to climb on your own. Luckily, there's a large stone block to the left that you can push in front of the ledge. Move to the side of it and hold the A button to interact and push it across until you can leap over to the other side.

Here you'll find one lit torch surrounded by three unlit braziers, and a few Deku Babas that you can kill to get more Deku Sticks if you're running low. Use one of the Deku Sticks to light on fire, then run between the three unlit braziers quickly so that all are lit at the same time, and the door will unlock itself.

Watch out for another ambushing Skulltula from above as you enter the next area, followed by three eggs falling from above that will quickly hatch to reveal Gohma Larva. These strange insects will stumble toward you and glow red before lunging at you, but tend to retreat when damaged. Fend them off by sidestepping or blocking their lunge and then retaliating.

With all enemies defeated, note the webbing in the top northwest corner of the room. Use the nearby lit torch to light up a Deku Stick so you can burn the webbing away, and defeat the Deku Baba and regular Skulltula guarding the path to the final Gold Skultulla of this dungeon. It's sitting high on some vines at the back of the room, and you can slingshot it before climbing up to get the token.

Returning to the area where you fought the larva, light up your Deku Stick once more to burn away the webbing to the east, and look for a small passage to crawl through, returning you to the first room you fell into in the basement.

From here, you'll find another large webbing blocking a hole in the ground, as well as a large stone block you can push forward and drop it down a ledge to create a shortcut back to the basement entrance -- and more importantly, the lit torch in the corner.

Jump down and pull out another Deku Stick, and light it up using the torch. Quickly hop back across the water to the block you pushed down, and jump up (with the stick still equipped) to pull yourself onto the ledge, and then roll into the webbing with the lit stick. If done quickly, the webbing will burn away, allowing you to drop down one more into the lower basement B2.

This area consists of one large room, guarded by the three Deku Scrubs that the other scrub warned you about earlier. He gave you a hint that defeating them was "as easy as two, three, one".

When approaching these Scrubs, you'll find that trying to bounce their nuts back at them won't work... unless it's done in the correct order. If you number the Deku Scrubs from left to right at 1, 2, 3, then defeating them means you'll need to stun them in the correct order. Dodge the incoming fire so that you only reflect the nuts back at the center Scrub first, then the one on the right, and finally the one on the left.

With the enemies defeated in the correct order, attack the final Scrub when it tries to flee, and it will impart some final wisdom before fleeing about defeating the boss. Be sure to search this room for some bushes you can slice up for more seeds and nuts as needed, and then head through the door to face the fearsome foe haunting the Great Deku Tree.

Link will find himself in a large darkened room with a strange clattering sound echoing forth. It may look empty at first, but you need only look upward to find the source - a large and malevolant eye, signaling the arrival of the boss.

Gohma is a heavily armored arachnid, and as the Deku Scrub warned, its only true vulnerable spot is that singular eye. This makes close combat battle a little harrowing, so you'll likely want to keep your distance until you spot your chance.

As she approaches, Gohma will cover her eyes with the mandibles above her face, and block any incoming attacks. Soon she will prepare to strike, raising its mandibles and two large forward claws. That's your cue to backflip away from the danger before Gohma slams forward.

As it slams down, you'll see that its claws get stuck in the dirt for a few moments. When the eye turns green with surprise, that's your cue to leap in and give its eye a single slash before its claws can break free, and then go back to playing defense until the next opening.

After a few strikes, Gohma will decide to change things up, and retreat away from you, and start climbing up the walls!

Watch it carefully, as soon after reaching the ceiling, Gohma's eye will turn green again. You need to be quick to react, and pull out your Fairy Slingshot to hit it with projectiles from afar while she remains out of reach.

If you don't attack fast enough, Gohma will begin to spawn a trio of larva to deal with. The good news is they'll drop down to the ground in egg form and hatch after several moments, giving you the chance to use your slingshot at range to rip apart the eggs before the larva can burst out.

Hitting its eye with your slingshot will cause Gohma to become stunned, crashing down to the ground and becoming dizzy for several moments. That's your cue to run in and start slashing with quick hits or jump attacks to deal as much damage as you can before Gohma can right herself and flee once more.

If you take too many hits from Gohma or her larva, be sure to run the length of the arena to spot a few Recovery Hearts to heal yourself with.

After recovering from her stunned state, Gohma may try to resume close combat attacks. You need only lure out her slam attack and then stab at the eye to stun her again, and keep landing blows. Do this about three times, and Gohma will be defeated! Your reward will be a special Heart Container, which gives you a full extra heart!

With your mission complete, head into the glowing blue light to talk to Navi, and teleport back outside.

The Great Deku Tree will thank you for your heroic duty, and reveal more about the world -- how the three Goddesses created the world, how the Triforce was created as they departed, and how an evil man seeks to claim its power by gathering the Sacred Stones that open the path to the Sacred Realm and Triforce.

Sadly, Link's heroism was not enough to save the Great Deku Tree from the spreading corruption. Imploring Link to take up his destiny to face this evil and protect the Triforce with the help of the Princess of Hyrule, the Great Deku tree will impart the Spirtual Stone of the Forest, the Kokiri Forest, before bidding on final farewell.

There's nothing more you can do here, so head back to Kokiri Forest to relay the news to a distraught Mido. Saria will also be upset at the thought of Link leaving the forest, and will leave.

You can talk to the rest of the Kokiri children to get their thoughts on the Deku Tree's passing, as well as stocking up on supplies at the shop if you wish. You can even return to Link's House whenever you wish to rest and recover your hearts!

When you're ready to set off on your grand adventure, leave the forest by way of the western exit, and speak to the Kokiri child guarding it, and he'll let you pass after learning of the Great Deku Tree's last request.

Before you can fully leave, you'll run into Saria. As a keepsake to remember her by, she'll gift you the Fairy Ocarina, a musical instrument that seems to hold some mystical power and will become important in your adventures. Your next task lies across the expansive Hyrule Field in Hyrule Castle itself, where a certain Princess is waiting to be found.

Up Next: The Princess of Hyrule Walkthrough

articles.title: The Princess of Hyrule Walkthrough - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains
articles.body:
Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains the same, there's plenty of new differences to be found while exploring Hyrule. Link has banished the evil beneath the Great Deku Tree and claimed the Spiritual Stone of the Forest, and destiny now calls him to leave the forest behind and seek out the Princess of Hyrule Castle.

Leaving the relative safety of the Kokiri Forest behind, Link has one last meeting with his childhood friend, Saria, who bestows upon him a Fairy Ocarina. You can play some tunes with it by pressing Left on the D-Pad, using the L, R, Y, X, and A buttons!

As you exit the forest and head up a wooded path, you'll come upon a vista overlooking the majestic Hyrule Field. This large expanse of land connects almost all of Hyrule's major regions, and though the region itself doesn't have too many points of interest, it does hold its share of creatures and secrets.

Before you can take your first steps, a strange and large talking owl named Kaepora Gaebora will swoop in above you, offering his counsel. He'll point out a small road leading northwest toward the distant Hyrule Castle, and the Castle Town situated on the other side of a small moat that you'll need to travel through to reach it. He'll also point out that you can reflect on your adventure by checking the Threads of Time. You can think of it as a sort of Quest Log that lists all active or completed quests - both major and minor, and a tapestry that fills itself out as you complete them. If you're ever unsure what to do next or what sidequests you can explore, be sure to check it out!

Note that unlike the original Ocarina of Time, time will not initially pass for your first journey through Hyrule Field, nor will the drawbridge leading to Hyrule Castle Town close. You're free to explore as much as you want without worry of day turning to night until after you have met the Princess.

While there's not a whole lot to do in Hyrule Field at the moment, there is something worth collecting early. As you start heading down the dirt path from the forest entrance, look for a lone and tall narrow tree perched on a hilltop to the west, overlooking a large ranch in the distance.

Cross the small stream to reach it, and then roll into the tree. Such narrow trees like this one often have items that can fall down from above (unlike larger gnarled trees), and this one in particular hides a Gold Skulltula to add its token to your collection!

While you're out here, you can also check out the large Lake Hylia to the south, or the desert entrance to Gerudo Valley further west, where Kaepora Gaebora will be stationed to give you some tips on the land (and nudge you back toward the castle). If you'd rather save those areas for later (which you probably should), take the main dirt path the owl showed you to head north to the castle. Along the way, you'll start running into creatures called Peahats. They float around and spin toward you with sharp leafy blades, but you can deflect them with your shield and then finish them off when they are stunned. If you want

Upon following the path to the north and reaching the castle town's moat, you can cross the imposing drawbridge and enter the town.

This bustling market town is nestled at the foot of the castle in the hills above, and is home to all manner of townsfolk and merchant shops. There's plenty to see and do here, so be sure to stop and talk to everyone to learn more about this strange new place.

Start by taking an immediate right into a room by the castle town gate, and you'll find an armory room littered with pots and crates, and one very bored guardsman. Liven things up by going to town and breaking all the pots you can -- trust us, he won't mind -- and you can stand to earn around 20 Rupees for doing so!

On top of that, you can also roll into the large crates by the guard at the far end of the room to find one is hiding a Gold Skultulla, which you can kill and claim its token.

Exit the armory and head down to the road to the main market plaza around a large fountain. There's a lot to take in here, so be sure to explore as much as you want. Note the two laughing men conversing by the fountain -- they will mention that one of them wanted to see the Princess and ended up getting stuck in a drainpipe, which sounds useful for our own goal of meeting the Princess.

Among the major points of interest here are an assortment of shops (though not all are up and running currently):

To the east is a Bazaar that sells a variety of goods, including a large Hylian Shield that can't be burned up by fire, but it is quite pricey (and there are other means of getting one).

Next to the Bazaar is the Potions Shop, and an old man out front will warn you that there's apparently a ruckus going on inside. Heading in, the shopkeeper will plead with you to help catch a wayward bug, and even give you your first Empty Bottle for free to do so! Simply equip it and press ZR when standing near the golden beetle to capture it. The shopkeeper will be so overjoyed, he'll fill your new bottle with a Red Potion that recovers all hearts! On top of this, the Potion Shop also sells all sorts of bottled goods should you have an empty bottle in need of refilling.

Just past the Potion Shop is a strange "Happy Mask Shop" that's not currently open for business, and a pathway leads up toward the fabeled Temple of Time. This large cathedral holds the secret entrance to the Sacred Realm, but you'll need all of the Sacred Stones first.

On the other side of the plaza across from the Happy Mask Shop, there's a Shooting Gallery you can partake in. For the cost of 10 Ruppees, you can try your luck at shooting all 10 targets using only 15 seeds with your Slingshot. Even if you only hit 8-9 targets, you'll get a free retry! Score a perfect 10, and you'll unlock a Bigger Deku-Seed Bag, increasing your ammo count to 40! You can also enroll in an Expert Course afterward, and can shoot for another perfect score to earn 30 Rupees each time.

The other shops along the east side and alleyway, the Bombchu Bowling Alley, Bombchu Shop, and Treasure Chest Shop are all closed for the time being. You can also find a man asking to buy bottled items from you, which include Bugs and Fish for a modest price.

Head up the main road up the hill toward the castle to continue on your way.

Arriving up at the entrance to Hyrule Castle, you'll again run into Kaepora Gaebora, who urges caution, as the castle guards likely won't just let you stroll in.

Sure enough, the main gate ahead is sealed, and the guard on duty will have none of your shenanigans and shoo you off.

Look on the right side of the road for a horse-drawn milk cart, and you'll find a young girl named Malon waiting nearby. Her father, Talon, owns Lon Lon Ranch, and apparently he's been out on delivery for some time, but has likely fallen asleep. Agree to help find him, and Malon will give you an item essential to waking Talon from his deep slumber: a Weird Egg.

Once you have the egg, look on the other side of a small water drain past the milk cart for bright green vines you can climb up onto a high ledge. Up here you'll find a strange stone that looks like an eye that will yelp the current time if you strike it, but it may hold other mysteries...

Follow the path up to another set of vines that allow you to climb up on top of the gatehouse. Move across the top and take a good look at the front gardens ahead of you. There are several soldiers stationed here, and while they don't move, they'll order you to halt and throw you out if you wander into their line of sight.

To avoid these guards, you can either risk jumping over the iron fence and behind the bushes before the closest guard spots you, or take a safe path up the main road, and then lean into the purple flowers to veer left before the road curves to avoid the guard.

From here, dart between the hedges by taking the middle path, and then hang around the outside to climb up the western wall to bypass the large locked gate.

Before climbing up the vines, look for a small enclosed area to the right with some barrels and sacks, and a lone tall and narrow tree. Roll into it, and you'll dislodge a Gold Skulltula from its hiding place!

Climb up the vines and head past another Sheikah Stone to reach the castle's main moat. There are two guards posted outside, but you can easily bypass them by jumping into the moat and swimming toward the tree on the far side. Note that the tree has a strange plant growing near it that you can't interact with yet, but it's worth remembering!

Just up the path from the moat is the sleeping form of Talon, owner of Lon Lon Ranch. By now, your Weird Egg should have hatched into a Wake-Up Cucco, so give it a test drive by presenting it to the sleeping man by pressing ZR when it's equipped.

Talon will jolt awake and introduce himself. Realizing he's left Malon all alone, he'll bolt for the exit, leaving behind his large milk crates.

If you remember what the two laughing men were talking about in the town, they mentioned getting stuck in a drainpipe -- the same one that's located right where Talon was sleeping. However, the leap to reach it is just a bit too high.

To solve this puzzle, start pulling the two milk crates over to where Talon slept, you can then push them one after the other of the ledge and into the recess below, with the second crate standing on top of the first, and giving you extra height to make the jump! Crawl through and head on into the castle grounds.

This next area is a more confined stealth section, in which you'll need to dodge more guards to reach the area that the Princess is in. If you get caught here, you'll automatically escape back to the drain entrance, so you don't have to worry about infiltrating the entire castle area all over again.

Climb up the ladder to get a vantage point for the first area, a fairly simple one. There's a lone guard watching the path through this area under a large gazebo. Luckily, some crates have been stacked on one side of the gazebo, which you can climb up and then carefully cross over the beam to the other side over his head.

Head up the stairs to overlook the next area: Two large hedges with two guards that patrol between them. Each will alternate moving from left to right, but won't fully walk to the right edge of the hedge. Use that to your advantage by waiting for the closest soldier to turn his back and then run up to the right side of the hedge and hide yourself in it, out of their line of sight.

Make sure the second guard has started moving back to the left before darting to the second hedge, and then onward to the final area.

Note that if you get close to their line of sight, the guards may pause to look in your direction. This can interrupt their normal patrol pattern, so make note of these delays when moving around them.

Entering a cellar area, you'll be atop an enclosed space with two large shelving area, and two more guards patrolling around them. This time, one guard will move in a counter-clockwise square route along the outside of the shelves, while the other stationary guard between the two shelves will alternate looking in both directions.

Wait until the soldiers has passed by the stairs leading down and turned away from you to quickly head down. You can either play fast and risky by heading up the left side -- pausing to wait for the middle guard to look to the right -- and beat the other patrolling soldier before he rounds the corner, or take things slow by following the moving guard at a distance to ensure he doesn't spot you, lagging behind his position a bit.

However you bypass the pair, you can run out the far door and hang a left to find the gardens where your objective lies.

On the other side of a beautiful courtyard garden, a young girl is peering through a window. As you approach, the girl will recognize that you have a fairy, and properly introduce herself as Princess Zelda of Hyrule.

After confirming that you indeed carry the Spiritual Stone of the Forest, you'll find that you're not the only with strange dreams. Princess Zelda appears to have the gift of prophecy, and has dreamed of a great calamity befalling Hyrule. The savior of this darkness appears from the light, carrying the Spiritual Stone and accompanied by a fairy.

Princess Zelda will tell more of the story of the Goddesses, the Sacred Realm, and of the Triforce, adding that the Temple of Time was built to guard the Sacred Realm, and can only be opened with the Spiritual Stones of the Forest, of Fire, and of Water. With each of these, the final key lies in the royal family heirloom, the Ocarina of Time!

Your task is to track down these remaining stones, and do so before evil forces can get ahold of them. That evil force happens to be what Zelda was spying on: Ganondorf, the King of the Gerudo Tribe hailing from the desert to the west.

In order to help you on your quest, the Princess will give you a new Key Item: Zelda's Letter, which should hopefully open up some pathways that would normally be closed to you.

After finishing your conversation with the Princess, she'll summon her attendant, a member of the Sheikah named Impa, to help you leave the castle.

Before you go, have you looked into the other windows of this courtyard? In the original game, you could sneak a peek of some famous Mario characters. Now however, you can find a large tapestry adorning the wall in the distance. Look closely, and you might recognize the Threads of Time! Spoiler Alert...

When you're ready to depart, speak to Impa, who has a gift for you. It is a song passed down the royal family, which also happens to serve as Zelda's Lullaby. Play it, and you will prove yourself to all within earshot that you are a messenger of the Royal Family:

Complete the prompt, and you'll officially learn Zelda's Lullaby, which will be added to your list of songs that you can review the notes of. You can also change the settings to play ocarina songs by humming or using musical instruments, which the Switch 2's built-in microphone will detect!

Leaving the castle behind, Impa will point you toward the imposing Death Mountain, where a race of beings called the Gorons guard the Spiritual Stone of Fire. At the mountain's base is Kakariko Village, and it's there you'll need to travel to ascend the mountain. It's also not a bad idea to check out the nearby Lon Lon Ranch, now that the owner has made his delivery to the castle...

Up Next: Spiritual Stone of Fire - Kakariko Village Walkthrough

articles.summary: Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains
articles.body:
Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains the same, there's plenty of new differences to be found while exploring Hyrule. After finally meeting Princess Zelda of Hyrule, Link has been enlisted to track down the remaining Spiritual Stones, starting with the Spiritual Stone of Fire held by the Gorons of Death Mountain.

To reach it, Link will first need to pass through Kakariko Village and learn more about the land, and there's also a quick detour to made a Lon Lon Ranch. Note that from this point on, the time of day will naturally flow from day to night, even if you're in a town (but the drawbridge leading back to Hyrule Castle Town will remain open at all times).

Before sprinting off toward Death Mountain, there's a quick but important detour to be made straight ahead of Hyrule Castle Town: Lon Lon Ranch. By now you've already met the owner Talon and his daughter Malon, and now that they're back on the ranch you can visit the place to see all of its features.

Getting around Hyrule Field as a child can be a bit taxing, and in the original N64 game you could move slightly faster by rolling. In the Remake, you can now simply hold A after rolling, and Link will start moving at a faster pace! Unlike some other Zelda games, this mode of travel will not drain any stamina!

Entering the ranch, you should first make your way directly past the buildings and over to the main part of the ranch housing all the horses in a large field (assuming its still daytime). In the middle, you'll find the girl Malon singing her iconic song to a young horse that will bolt away when you draw close.

Malon will introduce you to her "friend", whose name is Epona. Apparently she's very shy, but opens up when she hears the tune Malon sings. Malon will ask if you have and instrument to accompany her with, so oblige by pulling out your Fairy Ocarina. Follow along with her tune:

Enter the prompt, and you'll learn Epona's Song, and the horse will immediately come running!

Note that some Threads of Time, like "Malon's Friend", aren't entirely essential to complete your main story objectives, but are important side quests that you can start at any time, and complete them later in the story.

You can't do anything more with Epona for now since she's too small to ride (as are you), but there are a few other things to take note of in the ranch.

From the large field, head to the large crumbled tower in the far southwest corner of the ranch and head inside. There's a storage area here with nine milk crates, and a large metal grate at the end. Pull out the closest crates to empty two spots in the middle column, and then pull back the crate in the middle against the wall. This will reveal a small gap you can crawl through.

On the other side you'll find your first Piece of Heart! For every four pieces you find, you'll earn a new Heart Container to add to your total health!

If you speak to Malon again, she'll urge to to visit her father inside the main building. Another ranchhand, Ingo, can also be found in the stables in the smaller building, who seems really unhappy with his current lot in life, and blames it on the lazy owner. Sure enough, Talon is asleep amid a pile of chickens, but will wake up when you talk to him.

He'll offer to play a little game with you: Find all three of his "Super Cuccos" amid the gaggle of other Cuccos in the room. Find them all before time is up, and you'll win a prize: A bottle of Lon Lon Milk (including the bottle itself!).

The trick to finding them is to pay close attention to the mannerisms of the Super Cuccos. Compared to the regular ones, they are stiff and upright, wings angled down, and holding their heads high and flapping dramatically on occasion. Once Talon throws them into the group, look for their distinct animations to find them all quickly.

Win, and you'll get yourself a second Empty Bottle to use! The Lon Lon Milk will also heal a good amount in two servings, making it a good item to have when you get into danger.

Finally, be sure to check around the northeast side of the ranch, behind the main house Talon is in. There's a small yard area with a wooden tower, and two trees. Roll into the tall and narrow tree, and you can dislodge a Gold Skulltula here! There are others hiding on the ranch that come out at night, but you won't be able to get them just yet.

When you're ready to move on, exit the ranch and head to the northeast and up the stone stairs to Kakariko Village.

The sleepy village of Kakariko is quite peaceful and laid back compared to the bustling of Hyrule's Castle Town, but that doesn't mean there isn't a lot to do here.

The guard at the entrance will helpfully point you toward the biggest points of interest, and if you want to quickly get on your way to traverse Death Mountain, you need only take the stairs up to the left to find the sealed gate. However, there's plenty more to do here before moving on, so let's get started.

Most times, a Master Craftsman can be spotted by a large central tree yelling at his incompetent workers (at night his ill-tempered son will slink over instead) as they scurry around the village to build up a new structure on the right side of town. You can actually roll into the narrow tree to dislodge a Gold Skulltula!

Taking the right path up to the south past the building under construction, you can find a large home that used to belong to Impa, and has now been donated to the public. Below it is a distraught Cucco Lady, who seems to be missing all seven of her Cuccos! It's worth your while to help her out, so let's go over their hiding spots:

The first cucco is close by, in the construction site near the Cucco Lady herself, wandering around the scaffolding in the middle.

The second cucco is near the entrance to Kakariko Village itself, just by the gate.

The third cucco is inside a wooden crate near the center of town, on the side of the building where the lady cooking food for the village resides.

Before returning this cucco to the pen, bring it up to Impa’s house, and use it to glide down to the fourth cucco, which is found on top of the nearby pile of bricks.

The fifth cucco is found on the main path up towards Death Mountain Trail, heading north up the stairs past the tall wooden tower.

The next two cuccos are a bit harder to reach. Take any of the previous cuccos and bring it up to the windmill on the west side of town. Using the cucco you’re already holding, you can glide over this gap in the fence to reach the other side. Once over here, throw the cucco back over the fence so it doesn’t become stuck on this side. One of these Cuccos is on the other side, below the closed Potion House.

While you're here, be sure to look in for an open hole in the ground leading to a Grotto with a Treasure Chest holding 5 Rupees! After tossing the last two Cuccos over the fence toward the well so you can collect them, climb up the nearby ladder to a hilltop behind the windmill, where you'll find the final Cucco.

When you grab the Cucco on top of the hill behind the Windmill, make sure to leap over to the roof of Granny's Potion Shop (which is sadly closed for the time being). Carefully move to the other side of the blue roof closer to the wooden tower, and you'll find a man lounging on the lower roof section. He'll be so happy someone's come to see him that he'll give you a Piece of Heart!

When you've returned all seven Cuccos to the Cucco Lady, she'll award you a new Empty Bottle to keep, giving you even more room to store milk, potions, and bugs!

You may be wondering about the creepy cobweb-covered house on the north side of town below the Windmill. Enter it, and you'll find a horribly cursed family who have become half spider. Doomed by their greed, their only hope of being restored is by defeating the Gold Skulltulas that can be found all across Hyrule. For every 10 tokens you collect, you can earn new rewards (up to 50, and then a final reward for getting all 100):

At this point, it's a wise idea to always keep a Bug in one of your Bottles. If you ever run into a patch of soft soil, release a Bug into it, and it will force out a Gold Skulltula in hiding! Each soil patch contains one! You can usually find some hiding after cutting grass in areas like the garden plot near Impa's House, or the one just outside the village in Hyrule Field.

If you want to earn that first reward right now simply walk outside the Cursed Spider House and wait for nightfall. A small golden spiderweb just to the left of the door is its hiding spot, where the Gold Skulltula will appear only at night!

With 10 Gold Skulltula Tokens, return to the house, and speak to the leader of the family. He'll reward you with the Adult's Wallet, which allows you to carry around up to 500 Rupees at a time!

There are plenty of other Gold Skulltulas hiding around Kakariko Village, possibly due to the proximity to the cursed house:

Once night has fallen, inspect the building under construction on the south side of the village, near the Cucco Lady, and you'll find a Gold Skulltulla on a high ledge of the red brick wall, and you can use the scaffolding to reach it.

Another Gold Skulltula similarly only appears at night, and can be found along the ladder of the tall wooden tower in the center of town, along the pathway up to the Gate to Death Mountain. Hit it with your slingshot and then climb up to retrieve the token.

One final Gold Skulltula is hiding out of view, and likewise only appears at night. To the south of the wooden tower and Potion Shop is another building where a little boy lives (usually out playing in the graveyard), and if you circle around the back of the house, you can find a Gold Skulltula in its web along the building wall.

Aside from these major things, you're more than welcome to explore the village to your heart's content, including getting great views from the top of the tower, speaking to the loopy music guy in the Windmill Hut searching for the right song (which you don't have yet), or talking to the townsfolk.

When you head up the stepts to the gate to Death Mountain, a guard will inform you that the path is blocked on account of the danger of falling rocks, and none but those on important Royal business can proceed. Show him Zelda's Letter to change his tune (not that he takes it seriously), and he'll open the gate for you.

As a bonus, the guard will warn you about the falling rocks along the Death Mountain trail, and suggest you head to the Bazaar at Hyrule Castle Town to purchase a stronger Hylian Shield that won't burn away. He'll even put in a good word to discount the shield from 80 down to 60 Rupees. In return, he'll ask a small favor in checking out that new Happy Mask Shop that just opened, and seeing about getting a mask that he doesn't have the time to get himself.

We'll definitely want to make a detour back to Castle Town in a moment, but not because we need a discounted shield. In reality, there's a way to get a Hylian Shield without spending a single Rupee, and it lies further west past the Windmill...

The moody and foreboding Graveyard behind Kakariko Village holds the graves of the Sheikah Clan, guardians of the Royal Family that founded this village. There's a surprising amount of secrets to find here, hiding behind every gravestone!

By day, a small boy from the village will wander among the graves doing his best impression of the old gravedigger, Dampe, who only comes out at night. Annoyingly, if you try to interact with any of the graves, the kid will threaten to tattle.

At the very least, you can head up the steps on the left side to find a plot of soft soil on the other side of a small tree. Drop a Bug from your bottle (if you don't have one, look under the stones at the Graveyard entrance), and it will fish out a Gold Skulltula for you to defeat!

By night, Dampe the Gravedigger will wander the grounds, and despite the kid's threats during the daytime, he really doesn't care if you pull on any the headstones. What he does offer is Dampe's Heart-Poundin' Grave-Diggin' Tour!

Request to play Dante's Grave-digging tour, and he'll reveal several dirt mounds all across the graveyard area. You can guide him to any of the dirt mounds and interact with them to pay Dampe 10 Rupees to dig in the spot. Whatever comes up is yours to keep... provided something is actually buried there. Sometimes you'll get a few Rupees, other times nothing at all, but keep at it until he detects something heavy and asks for another 5 Rupees to keep at it, as it contains his special prize: A Piece of Heart!

As for the gravestones themselves, you can try pulling them from the back to reveal secrets: Some are empty, others can hold a Green Rupee, and some hold the restless dead known as Poes. These ghosts carry lanterns, and will turn invisible if you try and target them with ZL, before charging at you with their spinning lantern. Run away from the attack until they become visible, then sprint at them and roll after landing a hit to anticipate their retreat and strike again to finish them off.

When Poes are defeated, they'll leave behind their essence, which you can actually capture in a Bottle. Unfortunately, you don't know anyone who wants a Poe in a Bottle, and trying to "drink" them yourself will just poison your hearts.

A select few graves are actually hiding small tombs below, but the dangers within might be a little daunting at the moment. First, it's recommended to turn your attention to the large monuments at the back of the Graveyard. A large stone emblazoned with the royal crest is flanked by two other ornate graves in shape of harps.

Interact with them, and you'll summon one of two spirits: Sharp the Elder, and Flat the Younger. The spirits of these two Composer Brothers will attack on sight, much like any other Poe. This means you'll need to retreat and refrain from targeting them until they reveal themselves before dashing in to strike.

Once defeated, they'll both realize your not one of Ganondorf's agents and tell you their half of the story about how they were comissioned by the King of Hyrule to compose one half of a special song. When Ganondorf came looking to take this power, they hid its secret in the royal tomb nearby, where you can "prove yourself" as a royal envoy. Do so by standing on the crest and playing Zelda's Lullaby to open a dramatic entrance to this royal tomb, leading to A Song of the Royal Family.

Inside the tomb's first room, the doors will seal, locking you in combat with dangerous bats known as Keese. They hide in the walls until you draw close, then take to the air to start divebombing you. If you spot them early, take out your Slingshot to even the odds, or otherwise block their attack with your shield then slice when they turn to flee.

When all Keese in the room are rooted out and dealt with, continue into the next room. This creepy area is full of bubbling green goop that will damage you if you step into it. To make matters worse, terrifying undead known as Redeads stalk this room. If they spot you, they can let loose a shriek that will paralyze Link, and then stumble forward to latch on and steal your lifeforce until you can shake them off by mashing buttons.

There's a better way to deal with them, so for now, move slowly along the left side of the first bubbling pit, then dart along the middle to avoid the gazes of the two Redeads on the sides. Sprint out through the far door and into the next room.

At the far end, you'll find a poem inscribed on a stone plaque, and underneath will be a song you can commit to memory:

Complete the prompt, and you'll learn the Sun's Song! With this, you can turn day to night and night to day in the blink of an eye!

As you turn to leave, look along the crumbling pillars for a twinkling blue symbol you can have Navi inspect. It's Fairy Writing, left by another fairy, and may often have hints for you. In this case, the writing asks to hear the Sun's Song. Hints like these require you to play a specific song, and if you play the correct one, a Fairy's essence will spring out and fully heal you!

Return back to the previous room with the three Redead. Your Sun's Song has a secondary power - to put the restless dead to sleep. In this case, playing the song near these enemies will stun them for an extended period, allowing you to attack them without worry of being paralyzed or grabbed! Just make sure they are fully under the effects of the song before you assault them. Once they've been defeated, you can leave this area behind.

With the Sun's Song special power under your belt, it's time to dig up some more graves:

From the Graveyard entrance, head up the first small steps and look ahead among the first row of graves for the second to the top before the next stairway (where flowers have been planted and butterflies have gathered), and pull it back to reveal a tomb below. Unfortunately, the tomb's inside is sealed and you don't have the means to blast it open just yet.

Next, head up to the row of graves just before the steps up to the royal tomb. Pull back the second one on the right side of the pathway to reveal another tomb entrance. Inside is a Redead, but thankfully you have the Sun's power to stun it in it's tracks.

Defeat it, then open the Treasure Chest it was guarding to find a free Hylian Shield! No need to spend Rupees on this one!

Finally, pull back the grave at the far southern edge of this same row below the royal tomb, and you'll find one more tomb to drop into. No enemies here, but a large Treasure Chest holds a Piece of Heart -- which should be the fourth one you've found to grant you an extra Heart Container!

While you no longer need to buy a Hylian Shield, there's still a few things worth doing back at Castle Town if you have a moment to spare.

The Happy Mask Shop is now open for business, and follows a peculiar business model: You check out a mask at no initial cost as they become available, and then wear it when talking to people to gauge their interest. You can then sell it to an interested party, and then pay back the shop owner for the mask's original rate, regardless of how much you sold it for, and then check out the next mask to repeat the process!

Since you already know who's been asking for a mask, go ahead and check out the Keaton Mask, which normally has a value of 10 Rupees. You can then take it to the guard in Kakariko Village and sell it to him for 15 Rupees, earning a 5 Rupee profit when you pay the Mask Salesman back! You may also want to return and buy the Skull Mask next, since you'll have the chance to sell that one soon enough.

Before leaving Castle Town, wait around for nightfall, and look for the lady who's constantly doting on her little white dog named Richard. At this point, Richard will have gone missing, and you'll be tasked to find him amid all the other stray dogs that descend upon Castle Town in the evening.

To find Richard, head down the alleyway past the Bomchu Shop near where the lady and her dog live. Richard should appear around the back corner, not far from the Treasure Chest Shop (there are a few other white dogs in other parts of the alley, so you may grab the wrong one and need a do-over).

Interact with the dog to get it to follow you, then return to the lady. If it's the right dog, she'll be overjoyed and award you a Piece of Heart!

At this point, you've completed all the optional stuff that you possibly can thus far, and are in good shape to take the next step of your journey. With the gate opened, you can now leave Kakariko Village and take the trek up Death Mountain to visit Goron City and inquire about the Spiritual Stone of Fire.

articles.title: Spiritual Stone of Fire - Goron City and the Lost Woods Walkthrough - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains
articles.body:
Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains the same, there's plenty of new differences to be found while exploring Hyrule. After finally meeting Princess Zelda of Hyrule, Link has been enlisted to track down the remaining Spiritual Stones, starting with the Spiritual Stone of Fire held by the Gorons of Death Mountain.

Now that you've unlocked the gate to Death Mountain, it's time to undertake a dangerous trek up the mountain to meet the Gorons who live in the mountain. However, don't expect to gain their most prized possession so easily, and you may find your journey will soon lead you back to the Lost Woods in search of a dear friend.

Entering the harsh trail up Death Mountain, you'll need to be prepared to face new threats, and having the Hylian Shield equipped is a must. Though it's harder to wield, and requires you to stop moving to use if effectively, it allows Link to "turtle up" and hunker down to block all threats - even fiery ones!

Your first such threat is an enemy called a Red Tektite. These spider-like creatures jump high in an attempt to pounce on prey, but will bounce off your shield, allowing you to retaliate with a few quick stabs.

Defeat the other Red Tektites in the area to climb up a mesh wall to a higher ledge. Here you'll find a large blocked cave, and a curious balled up creature. This is a Goron, and he's pretty friendly (and also hungry). You can ask him about a few things, and he'll explain that their food source in Dodongo Cavern nearby has now been sealed up and point you further up the mountain path to where his friends are.

Continue your climb, and watch out for a rolling Goron (he can't actually hurt you, but can knock you down!). Further past him is a trail leading to the top of the mountain that's blocked off by large rocks, so instead take a sharp left for a tunnel path leading toward Goron City.

Near the entrance, you can find a Goron overlooking a strange looking plant. It's called a Bomb Flower, and as it name implies, it will explode shortly after being picked up. Unfortunately, your child limbs lack the strength to pick it up right now, so continue on into the city itself.

Note that there's a small alcove to the right of the city entrance with another of those strange plants with curved leaves. Nearby, you can find a Fairy Writing that indicates strong weather may cause the leaves to spin. Sounds like a clue worth remembering!

The City of Gorons is a large underground region comprised of several descending tiers around a large recessed pit in the middle of the city. The Chieftain of the Gorons dwells at the very bottom, and high above you can spot a series of rope bridges leading to some sort of altar.

Make your way over to the altar by heading right and then crossing the bridges to talk to the Goron here, who was apparently looking for a "tasty red stone" but Boss Darunia probably took it, and has holed himself up in his quarters. Sounds like a Spiritual Stone!

You won't be able to access much of the city due to the large rocks in the way, so head down to the lower level, past a rolling Goron who doesn't want to stop (and you lack the tools to make him), and down one more level to where a Goron is wisftully listening to some familiar music through a crack in the wall.

On the other side of this level is a pathway down to a spot you can rest at, and a Goron who can't believe you're from a place with lots of greenery. The only green things he's seen are Bomb Flowers and Deku Sticks, which are rare as they use them to light bomb flowers. It's worth stockpiling them, and if you're running low, check the pots next to him for a stick you should hang onto.

Continue on to the bottom floor where a giant Goron-shaped pot, and just beyond it are two sealed rooms - one covered in bomb flowers, and the other bearing the Triforce on a mat. Since you're technically a messenger of the Royal Family, announce yourself by playing Zelda's Lullaby, and you'll be granted access to speak with the "Boss", Darunia.

The bad news is Darunia is in a terrible mood: An ancient beast is loose in Dodongo Cavern, halting the harvest of both bomb flowers and their food supply. If you want answers, you're going to need to improve Darunia's disposition.

Stepping back outside his room, talk to the nearby Goron, who mentions that Big Bro has a favorite song that might improve his mood. However, his singing is... not easy to follow. You'll need a better source to follow along with on your Ocarina, and luckily, you've already heard the music coming from nearby.

Even if you couldn't convince Darunia, you did gain access to the two torches in his room, which means you can transfer that fire elsewhere with a Deku Stick if you're quick enough. Start by lighting a Deku Stick and running into the next room to light up a Bomb Flower next to the sealed up door. It will explode, revealing a Goron Shop for you to browse.

Unfortunately, most of what this Goron sells can't be used yet, including a heaping helping of bombs, and an adult-sized Goron Tunic. Next, take the lit Deku Stick from Darunia's chambers and make a lap around the giant Goron-shaped pot, lighting all four torches here before putting your Deku Stick away so it doesn't burn. This will also set the pot spinning, which you can interact with later.

Finally, light up your Deku Stick using the torches around the pot and up to the next level. Head toward the large cracked wall where the music is coming from and light the bomb flowers with your Deku Stick. This will blast open a secret shortcut leading back into the depths of Kokiri Forest...

Entering a mystical forest, you'll meet up with Kaepora Gaebora again, who will clue you in about the origins of the song that seems to float through these woods. You'll find the source at the Sacred Grove, but it's easy to lose your way in these woods.

The trick to navigating this maze of a forest is the music. When you approach any darkened tunnel entrance, listen carefully: If the music fades away, you'll have chosen wrong, and continuing will just send you back to the start. If the music continues softly, you're on the right track (you'll also see musical notes play as you head through the tunnel). Take a wrong turn, and you'll find yourself back in Kokiri Woods!

There's also a good amount of secrets to uncover, but for now, you'll want to reach the Sacred Grove first. From the Goron City shortcut, head left (East), then left again when you reach the area with the pool of water.

Continue straight through the next 4-way intersection to reach an area with a single boulder, and head left, and then take a right at the next area with another single boulder, and you'll have arrived at your destination.

The dense forest has now opened up into a large open grove, but there's still more twists and turns left to take. Before you can truly enter the grove, you'll need to defeat its guardian: A Wolfos.

These powerful monsters will fight shrewdly and evasively, preferring to strafe around you and find an opening. When they dash forward, the Wolfos will slash twice with its claws. If you hunker down and shield the blow, it will bounce back momentarily before trying again, buts its claws also give it a lot of protection.

Instead, wait for it to begin its two-hit lunge and backflip away. After its second swipe, it will overswing and reveal its back, which has a scarred weak point you can strike at with a jump attack! Keep up these counterattacks to defeat this foe, and the gate will open.

The next part of the grove is a maze of zig-zagging passages, guarded by Mad Scrubs. These Deku Scrubs are more aggressive, shooting a salvo of three Deku Nuts at a time. You can still block the nuts by shielding up, and the third nut will bounce back into it, causing it to flee a short distance.

Take out the scrubs as you proceed along the route and around a large square area with watery holes in the corners to reach a final narrow path to the end of the grove. More Scrubs are here, but you can snipe them at a distance with your Slingshot to send them running.

At the top of the stairs, you'll finally find the source of the music: your friend Saria. She's happy to see you, and even though your journey means you can't come home yet, she's found a way to communicate with you by playing her special song, which you can now follow along on your Ocarina:

Follow the prompts to learn Saria's Song, which marks you a friend of the forest, and can make even the grumpiest of Gorons dance with delight. It will also allow you to talk to Saria no matter where you are, and she may have advice or tips to give you depending on your location when you call for her using the song.

It's time to head back, and as you head back down the stairs, note the opening in the large walls at the base to find a hole in the ground you can drop into. This leads to a Fairy Fountain, which you can interact with to fully heal yourself, or catch one in a bottle. If you fall in battle that Fairy will restore some of your hearts so you can keep fighting!

Once you're back in the Lost Woods, it's time to see what the rest of the maze has to offer. Start by taking an intentional wrong turn into Kokiri Forest.

Look around the back of the Kokiri Shop, and you should be able to spot a patch of soft soil. Plant a bug in it, and a Gold Skulltula will jump out for you to slay.

Use the Sun's Song to make sure it's nightfall in the forest, and then check around the back of the Home of the Know-It-All Brothers by the Training Grounds. It's here you'll find a new Skulltulla hiding along the treehouse wall.

Now, head back into the Lost Woods, and from the starting point, take a left. This leads to a small grove with a friendly Skull Kid playing on his flute. Step onto the smaller trunk, and play Saria's Song with him. Any friend of Saria's is a friend of him, and he'll reward this new bond with a new Piece of Heart for you!

While you're here in front of the Skull Kid, you should try wearing the Skull Mask that the Happy Mask Salesman rents out after selling the Keaton Mask. The Skull Kid will take an immediate liking to the mask, and offer to buy it from you. Unfortunately, he'll only pay to 10 Rupees, which means you'll have to eat the full cost when paying the Happy Mask Salesman back (You may also want to hang onto the mask for a bit first until you find the Forest Stage in the Lost Woods).

From this grove with the solitary Skull Kid, be sure to move south through a nearby tunnel. It will take you to a high ledge overlooking the bridge leading out of Kokiri Forest, and you can find some soft soil here. Drop another bug in if you have one, and out will pop another Gold Skulltulla to defeat.

Be sure to drop down into the ravine below the bridge, and run over to the far side. There's a new type of Deku here, a Business Scrub. They act much like Deku Scrubs, but when defeated, they'll be bullied into selling you wares they have procured. This particular Business Scrub has a Bigger Deku-Stick Bag that he will sell you for 40 Ruppes, allowing you to carry a maximum of 20 from now on, and you should take the deal!

Return to the Lost Woods entrance, and this time follow the music right to the east. This next area has a lower pathway, but before jumping down, look for a large target carved out of a tree ring. Stand on the nearby trunk, and hit the exact center of the target three times. If succesful, a Deku Scrub will congratulate you, and spit the Biggest Deku-Seed Bag at you, giving you a maximum of 50 shots!

Now, jump down to the bottom where two more Skull Kids are playing their instruments on large tree trunks. Join with them using your Ocarina, and they'll start a game of "follow the tune". You'll need to repeat a randomized tune of notes that build from 3-5, and if you can follow along, they'll pass you a Blue Rupee.

Try it again, and this time you'll have to follow the notes that build from 4-6. If you're having trouble as they hide which notes you need to memorize, look for the placement on the prompt to clue you in on which notes you need to remember. Complete this task, and you'll earn a Red Rupee worth 20.

Play their game one last time for a super hard version of following notes that build from 6 to 8. If you can keep following along, you'll earn the ultimate prize: a new Piece of Heart!

Finally take the path north to where the shortcut to Goron City is. This time, head right to the pool of water, then left going north, and take another left. This will lead you to a smaller meadow teeming with several Business Scrubs. Block their attacks to make them docile, and you can browse their normal wares.

The more important points of interest lie near the back of the grove by the bushes. On the side near a large tree is some soft soil, which you can again drop a Bug into (one of the scrubs actually sells Bugs!) to reveal the last Gold Skulltula that you can get for now in this area.

There's also a hole hidden in the bushes you can drop down, revealing an underground Forest Stage. By standing on the platform and wearing a mask, a group of Deku Scrubs will judge your appearance and give you random rewards... or attack you. However, if you wear that Skull Mask again (if you sold it to the Skull Kid you can always rent it again), a larger Scrub will emerge to award you the Biggest Deku-Stick Bag!

With all your tasks completed in the woods, return to the shortcut back to Goron City.

You can now return to Darunia and play him the song of your people: Saria's Song. The mood to dance will overtake the Big Boss of the Gorons, and put on a mighty display of getting down to the beat. Once he's finished, he'll finally be ready to hear you out, and though he's not willing to give away the Spiritual Stone of Fire for free, he will reward you for helping him clear out Dodongo's Cavern of its monster infestation.

To help you in this matter, he'll give you a special gift: The Goron Bracelet. With this, you'll be able to harvest Bomb Flowers yourself and use them to blow up cracked stones that may be blocking your way!

The few Bomb Flowers left in Goron City aren't enough to really make use of, but you can test it out on the top ring of the city, to the east of the entrance. Look for a large cracked wall next to some Bomb Flowers, and pick up then toss them with R and stand clear as the detonate. You'll have to toss them at a few cracked walls to open up a path to a very large Medigoron. He's working on a special weapon, but it'll take a few years to finish...

Now, Exit Goron City back onto the Death Mountain Trail. Head over to the Goron babysitting the lone Bomb Flower, and try grabbing it. You can then toss it over the ledge and down toward the large cracked boulder blocking the entrance to Dodongo Cavern, which will explode to reveal its entrance!

Before heading in, note the patch of soft soil just inside the tunnel, and drop a Bug inside to scare out a Gold Skulltula that you can defeat for a token.

With the way clear, it's time to earn the Spiritual Stone of Fire by delving into the depths of Dodongo Cavern.

Up Next: Dodongo Cavern Dungeon Walkthrough
